The Pūrvārcika, the Chanda-ārcika, and the Āgneya-kāṇḍa.
First Prapāṭhaka. First Half.
1.1.1.0101a O Agni, come hither for the feast, being praised for the giving of the oblation.
O Agni, you have been appointed as the Hotṛ-priest of all sacrifices among the gods for the human race. We choose Agni as our messenger, the all-knowing Hotṛ-priest.
1 1 1 0103c Of this sacrifice, [the one] of skillful intellect...
3 1 1 1 0104a May Agni, seeking wealth, strike down the Vṛtras with his inspired praise; 1 1 1 0104c well-kindled, bright, and invoked with oblations... 4
I praise for you the most beloved guest, dear like a friend— Agni, who is to be known like a chariot.
O Agni, with your great powers, protect us from every hostile force.
Or [the wrath] of the mortal enemy...
Come here, O Agni; let me speak these other songs to you.
May you grow strong by means of these drops of Soma.
May Vatsa direct your mind hither, even from the most distant dwelling-place;
O Agni, I desire you with my song.
O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the lotus-leaf.
From the head of the entire world, O priest...
O Agni, bring forth radiantly for us great protection;
for you are a god for us to behold.
O Agni, the peoples sing praise to you for your power, O God;
with your weapons, crush the enemy. [I praise] your messenger, the all-knowing, the immortal bearer of oblations.
I adorn with my song the one most worthy of sacrifice. Toward you, the sisters— the songs that point the way and prepare the oblation—
have taken their stand in the presence of Vāyu.
Day by day, O Agni, we approach you with our thought, O dispeller of darkness; bringing homage, we come to you.
O you who are awakened by praise, take note of that for every people, for the one worthy of sacrifice.
1. A beautiful hymn for Rudra... 15.
You are invoked to this lovely sacrifice for the sake of protection; O Agni, come with the Maruts! 16. [Verse fragment]... O Agni, come with the Maruts!
I shall worship you, Agni, with prostrations, like a horse that brings desirable wealth—
the sovereign lord of sacrifices.
Like Aurva, Bhr̥gu, and Apnavāna, I call upon the pure one.
1.1.1.0208c Agni, whose garment is the ocean...
18 1.1.1.0209a The mortal kindling Agni with his mind should attend upon his inspired thought (dhi).
1.1.1.0209c He kindles Agni with the rays of light. 19
From the beginning, they behold the light of the ancient seed, the morning radiance which is kindled high in heaven.
[I praise] Agni for you, the most abundant, who increases the sacrifices.
To the powerful grandson [of strength],
may Agni with his sharp flame strike down every devourer;
may Agni win wealth for us.
O Agni, be gracious; you are great. You have come to this god-seeking people to sit upon the sacred grass (*barhis*).
O Agni, protect us from distress; O God, strike down those who seek to harm us.
O Agni, burn with your most scorching flames, ageless one... 24 O divine Agni, yoke those well-trained horses of yours; swift-moving, they carry you readily. 25

O Lord of the People, we meditate upon you, the radiant one, worthy of being reached, the possessor of heroic sons, O Agni, when you are invoked with oblations. Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth.
He quickens the seeds of the waters...
27 O Agni, do thou proclaim this our newest gain, this Gāyatra song, among the gods. 28
O Agni, Aṅgiras, Gopavana has generated you with his song; as such, O Purifier, hear our invocation. Agni, the sage and lord of booty, has stepped around the oblations.
Bestowing jewels upon the donor...
His rays bear aloft that god Jātavedas,
the Sun, so that everyone may behold him.
Praise Agni, the seer, whose laws are true, at the sacrifice—the god who drives away disease.
May the goddesses be auspicious for our aid; may they be auspicious for our drinking.
May they flow toward us for our well-being and prosperity...
33 Whose prayers do you now fulfill? You quicken them, O Lord of the Good.
May he whose songs you take pleasure in [be successful]... 34
Sacrifice after sacrifice with song after song, for your Agni, so that he may be skillful.
We shall praise the immortal Jātavedas more and more, like a dear friend.
O Agni, protect us with your first [form], and protect us also with your second.
Protect us with three songs, O Lord of Strength; protect us with four, O Vasu.
With your lofty flames, O Agni, with your bright radiance, O God—kindled by Bharadvāja, O Most Youthful One—shine forth, O Purifier, bestowing wealth.
O Agni, well-invoked with *svāhā*, may the wise patrons (*sūrayaḥ*) be dear to you—
those generous lords of people who open up the stall of cattle for us.
O Agni, singer, lord of the clans, burning away the demons, O god...
1.1.1.0405c O Householder, you are great; you do not depart, the protector of heaven, dwelling in the home.
39 1.1.1.0406a O Agni, immortal one, bring splendid wealth from the radiant dawn.
1.1.1.0406c O Jātavedas, bring today the gods who awaken at dawn to the donor. 40
O Vasu, with your wondrous aid, impel riches toward us.
O Agni, you are the charioteer of this wealth; find a firm footing for our offspring.
You alone, O Agni, are far-extending, the protector, the seer of Truth.
The wise sages, the ordainers, seek to win you over, O kindled and radiant one.
O Agni, Purifier, grant us wealth that increases our vitality and is worthy of praise; and through your excellent guidance, bestow upon us that which is most desired and brings the highest renown.
He who distributes all wealth, the joyous invoker of men— for him,
as for the first vessels of honeyed mead, let our hymns of praise go forth unto Agni.
With this reverence, I invoke for you Agni, the Son of Strength.
The most beloved, the most mindful, the delight of the well-performed sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all—45 You lie within the forest trees, your mothers; mortals kindle you together.
Unwearied, you carry the oblation of the preparer of the offering; from there, you reign among the gods. 46
He has been seen, the best finder of the path, in whom they have established their sacred vows.
May our songs of praise reach Agni, the newborn, the strengthener of the noble one.
Agni is the high priest at the hymn of praise; the pressing-stones and the sacrificial grass are at the rite.
With a *ṛc* I seek the Maruts, O Brahmaṇaspati; O gods, grant us excellent protection. (48) Praise Agni with songs for his aid, him whose flame is piercing.
O Purumīḍha, men praise Agni for wealth; Agni [grants] a dwelling for well-being. (49)

Hear us, O Agni, you whose ear is keen, together with the gods who are your companions and who travel at dawn. Let Mitra and Aryaman sit upon the sacrificial grass at this rite, along with those who come at early morning.
Agni, the god of Divodāsa, is like Indra in his majesty.
Following after his mother Earth, he has spread himself out; he stands upon the protection of the firmament.
Now from the earth, or from the shining realm of the great heaven, grow strong with this body and my song; O you of noble wisdom, fill us with the things born of your power.
When you, O Agni, were being fashioned from the woods, you drank the waters of the mother earth;
that turning back of yours, O Agni, which occurred while you were far away yet became manifest here, cannot be forgotten. Manu established you, O Agni, as a light for all people forever.
Kaṇva, born of *ṛta*, has beheld you, the grown one whom the peoples revere.
First Prapāṭhaka, Second Half:
May the god Draviṇodas desire for you the full ladle as it is poured out.
1.1.2.0601c Rise up! Resound! Or fill [the vessels]! Then indeed the god honors you. 1.1.2.0602a Let Brahmanaspati go forth; let the goddess Sūnṛtā go forth.
1.1.2.0602c Toward the heroic, manly one who bestows fivefold gifts—may the gods lead our sacrifice. 56.
Stand up for our protection like the god Savitṛ;
standing erect, you are the winner of booty when we, the singers, invoke you with ointments.
The mortal who desires to lead him toward wealth, O Vasu, shall offer worship to you.
He himself, O Agni, supports the hero who recites the hymns, he who possesses a thousandfold prosperity.
We choose with well-spoken words the mighty Agni among many tribes who seek the gods— the one whom others kindle with fuel.
This Agni rules over heroic vigor and good fortune;
he rules over wealth consisting of noble offspring and cattle; he rules over the slaying of Vṛtra.
O Agni, you are the lord of the house; you are our Hotṛ-priest at the sacrifice.
You are the boat, O possessor of all boons, the wise one; you fashion and go toward that which is desirable.
We mortals have chosen you as our friend, O God, for our protection—the Son of the Waters, the blessed one, of wondrous deeds, the swift victor, the peerless one.
Offer the oblation; purify [the fire] with the sacrificial gift; establish the Hotṛ-priest as the master of the house.
At the place of Iḍā, honor with reverence him to whom offerings are given; worship him, the sacrificer of the dwellings.
Wondrous indeed is the growth of the young infant, who does not follow his two mothers for the sake of suckling.
When she who has no udder gave birth, he indeed grew strong as soon as he was born, immediately undertaking the great office of messenger.
This is one light for you, and beyond that is another; unite with the third light.
Be pleasant for your own body when entering [the womb], dear to the gods in the highest place of birth.
1.1.2.0704a Let us fashion this hymn with our intellect for the worthy Jātavedas, as one fashions a chariot.
1.1.2.0704c For his providence is auspicious for us in the assembly; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
1.1.2.0705a [We praise] Agni Vaiśvānara, the head of heaven, the messenger of earth, born in the Eternal Order (ṛta).
The gods, drawing near, generated as their vessel the sage, the sovereign, the guest of men.
From thee, O Agni, the gods generated [thee] with hymns, as waters flow from the back of a mountain.
Thee, such as thou art, our songs and fair praises urge forward, even as horses that carry the singer win the race.
Bring hither for your protection Agni, the king of the sacrifice, the Rudra, the invoker of the two worlds, the priest who sacrifices truly;
bring him, who is golden-hued, before the unperceived thunderbolt strikes. The king, the victor in battle, is kindled with prostrations—he whose face is anointed with clarified butter.
Men, pressing forward with their offerings, praise Agni; he has blazed at the forefront of the dawns.
With his lofty banner Agni advances; like a bull, he bellows toward the two worlds.
He has reached the very limit of heaven; the buffalo has grown great in the lap of the waters.
O men, with your insights, generate from the two fire-sticks the praiseworthy Agni, who is moved by the hands; him who is visible from afar, the lord of the house, the tireless one.
Agni has been awakened by the fuel of the people, facing the approaching Dawn like a cow.
Like young birds springing up to the branch, his rays stream forth toward the firmament.

The mighty one, the conqueror, the great sustainer of wisdom, the wise one who is not deluded, the destroyer of forts—he leads the forest with his songs and inspires the prayer. Like one with a golden beard, he shines with wealth through his armor.
One of your forms is bright, the other is worthy of sacrifice; you are like the sky, possessing two days of different aspects.
For you protect all wondrous powers, O self-dependent one; O Pūṣan, may your bounty here be auspicious.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the nourishment of the cow, a gift of many wonders, and most enduring.
May there be for us a son, a progeny who continues the lineage; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be with us.

Born as the great Hotṛ-priest, the knower of the vast space, he has sat down in the gathering place of men at the turning point of the waters—he who, established in the pressed juice, bestows vital strengths, the controller of riches for the worshipper, and the protector of our bodies.

Let the one who praises call upon the sovereign, the praised Asura, the man to be celebrated by the peoples—the deeds of Indra, the mighty one, as they are performed; let those who offer praise desire to enter through the doors of worship.
Jātavedas has been deposited in the two fire-sticks, like a well-nourished embryo within pregnant women.
Day after day Agni is to be praised by watchful men who bring oblations.
O Agni, from of old you have crushed the sorcerers; the *rakṣases* have never conquered you in battles. Burn up the devouring ones along with their roots; let none escape your divine missile.
O Agni, bring to us the most powerful splendor, O you who are irresistible! Open for us a path toward wealth most worthy of praise and toward strength.
If a mortal hero should follow [this way], he shall kindle the fire.
Offering the oblation continuously, may he enjoy divine protection.
Your brilliant smoke rises up; it spreads white and vast across the sky. For like the sun in its brilliance, O Purifier, you shine with your radiant form.
For you, O Agni, possess a fame worthy of a ruler; like Mitra, you exercise lordship.
O all-seeing Vasu, you nourish renown as if it were prosperity.
At dawn, let Agni, the beloved guest, be praised by many.

In whom, the immortal, all mortals kindle the oblation— sing a great song for that Agni, O Vibhāvasu, which is most effective in carrying [the offerings]. Like a sovereign queen, wealth and spoils of war arise from you.
Seeking strength, we praise with hymns of power your Agni, the beloved guest of every house,
the lord of the dwelling. Sing a lofty song for the radiant god Agni.
The mortal men have not placed that friend before them for praise.
We have come to Agni, the slayer of Vṛtra, the eldest, the descendant of Manu—
he who, O Śrutarvan, is kindled with great splendor at the home of Ṛkṣa.
Born by the highest law (*dharman*) together with those who have grown old, Agni is the father of Kaśyapa; Śraddhā is the mother, and Manu is the sage. We take hold of King Soma, Varuṇa, and Agni.

Āditya, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Brahmán, and Bṛhaspati—these have ascended from here; they have climbed to the ridges of heaven. Like the victorious Bhūrijayas, the Aṅgirases have gone forth upon the path to the firmament.
O Agni, we kindle you for great wealth and for the sake of giving. Praise the Bull for the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth;
for he has indeed been let loose, and when one proclaims of him, "He is the Brahman," that is truly so.
He has encompassed all poetic wisdoms as the felly encompasses the wheel.
O Agni, with your heat, crush the heat [of the enemy] on every side;
humble the strength and subdue the power of the sorcerer and the demon.
O Agni, worship here the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas;
sacrifice for the person who performs the rite well, the one born of Manu, who sprinkles the clarified butter.
Second Prapāṭhaka, First Half.
O Agni, I, your friend, have spoken much to you as one who offers oblations; indeed, [I am] yours.
Like the shelter of a great impeller, [be mine].
Bring forth the ancient, lofty word for Agni, the Hotṛ-priest.
To the ordainer who bears the lights of the waters...
O Agni, lord of booty consisting of cattle, O son of strength,
bestow upon us great renown, O Jātavedas!

O Agni, most skilled in sacrifice, worship the gods at the rite for the one who seeks the gods. As the joyous Hotṛ, you shine forth and drive away our adversaries. Having been born from the seven mothers, he has bestowed wisdom for the sake of glory.
This [god] is the constant lord of riches; may he take notice of us. And may Aditi come to us with her aid by day;
may she grant us peace and well-being, driving away our enemies.
Praise him indeed for his responsiveness; worship Jātavedas, whose smoke wanders abroad and whose radiance is ungraspable. No mortal enemy shall prevail over him by means of magic.
Whoever has offered oblations to Agni, the giver of sacrificial offerings...
[drive] away that crooked enemy, the thief, O Agni, who is evil-minded;
O Lord of the Good, make his path most distant and provide us with a fair way.
O Hero, O Lord of the People, Agni, listen with favor to this new hymn of mine;
burn down the guileful Rākṣasas with your heat. Sing forth to the most generous one, the observer of Truth, the lofty one of brilliant luster.
1.2.1.0201c Praised with hymns for Agni...
107 1.2.1.0202a He, O Agni, overcomes by means of your protections, which bring heroic sons and are effective in winning the prize;
1.2.1.0202c he whose friendship you have guarded. 108
1.2.1.0203a Glorify him, the hero of heaven; the gods have established him as the divine messenger.
1.2.1.0203c He shall carry the oblation to the gods.
109 1.2.1.0204a Do not be angry with our guest; Agni is the benevolent one, praised by many.
He who is the excellent invoker, skilled in the sacrifice...
May Agni, when invoked, be auspicious for us; may his gift be auspicious, O fortunate one, and may the sacrifice be auspicious.
And may our praises be auspicious.

We have chosen you, the most excellent sacrificer, the immortal god among the gods, the priest of this sacrifice, the one of noble wisdom. O Agni, bring us that splendor which, in our dwelling, shall overcome every devouring demon.
He [averts] the wrath of the evil-minded person... When the Lord of the People, the keen and well-pleased Agni, bestows [favor] upon the human clan, he repels all the *rakṣas* demons.
Thus ends the Āgneya section of the Kāṇḍa; now the Aindra Kāṇḍa:
Sing this for you at the libation for the one invoked by many, the heroic warrior.
1.2.1.301c That which is auspicious for the powerful bull...
1.2.1.302a O Śatakratu Indra, that most glorious exhilaration which is yours— 1.2.1.302c with that, indeed, do you now rejoice in the intoxication. 116
The two cows lowed at the pit, the great bestowers of abundance for the sacrifice; both their ears are made of gold. Sing, O Śrutakakṣas, for the horse and for the bull.
1.2.1.304c: [It is] worthy of Indra’s abode... 118 1.2.1.305a:
We incite that Indra for the sake of slaying the great Vṛtra.
1.2.1.305c: May he become the bull, the showerer of blessings. 119
O Indra, you were born from strength, from power, and from vigor; O bull, you are indeed the bull among those who possess bulls.
The sacrifice magnified Indra when he spread out the earth.
Fashioning a crest upon the sky...
O Indra, if I were the sole lord of wealth just as you are,
then my praiser would be one who possesses cattle.
O pressers, run hither for the sake of exhilaration, bringing every kind of merchandise—Soma for the hero, for the brave one! O Vasu, drink this pressed juice; fill your belly completely.
1 2 1 0310c These [are] your fearless ones... 124 1 2 1 0401a Toward the one renowned for his greatness, the bull of heroic deeds, 1 2 1 0401c as a shooter you go, O Sūrya. 125
O Vṛtra-slayer, whatever the sun has risen over today, all that is under your power, O Indra. You who,
by your skillful guidance, brought Turvaśa and Yadu from afar.
May that youthful Indra be our friend... (127) O Indra, do not turn us away from the quarters; may the Sun restrain us within his rays. With you as our ally, may we win that... (128)
O Indra, bring us wealth that wins the prize, victorious, ever-conquering,
most excellent for our protection.
We invoke Indra in the great battle, and Indra in the small conflict.
The wielder of the thunderbolt, the ally against the Vṛtras... (130) Indra drank the pressed juice of the *kadru* plant at the *sahasrabāhva* [sacrifice]; there he displayed his manly prowess.
O Indra, O Bull, we who long for you sing our praises aloud;
O Vasu, take note of us here.
Indeed, those who kindle the fire and spread the sacrificial grass in due order—
Those for whom Indra is a youthful friend... Break asunder all enemies; strike down the oppressors and the mockers.
Bring us that desirable wealth.
Right here we hear them as they speak, the whips held in their hands; they prepare their brilliant course for the journey.
O Indra, these Soma-offering friends of yours look out for you.
As those possessing nourishment [seek] their cattle...
all the tribes, all the peoples, bow down before his wrath,
as rivers flow toward the ocean.
We choose that great exhilaration of the gods for ourselves,
the protection of the bulls for our aid. O Brahmaṇaspati, make us hear the sounds of the Soma juices.
May Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij...
may he who is mindful awaken for us; may the slayer of Vṛtra, who has many libations, hear our prayer, O Śakra.
O God Savitṛ, today bestow upon us prosperity accompanied by progeny;
drive away evil dreams. Where is his bull, the youthful one, with powerful neck and unbending strength?
Who honors that Brahmā? In the secret recesses of the mountains and at the confluence of the rivers,
the sage was born through inspired thought.
Let the singer praise with new songs Indra, the sovereign lord of the peoples, the hero who overcomes men, the most bountiful.
Second Prapāṭhaka. Second Half.

The jaws of the powerful Indra, who is well-skilled and offers the oblation, have drunk of the soma-juice mixed with barley. O Lord of abundant wealth, these songs of praise have resounded toward you.
Like milch-cows lowing for their calf, [the seers found the name].
Here they discovered the secret name of Tvaṣṭṛ,
right there in the dwelling of the moon.

When Indra, the most vigorous bull, brought down the great waters from the mountain, Pūṣan was there as his companion. The cow, seeking glory, yields her milk for the Maruts; she is the mother of the bounteous ones.

1 2 2 0605c The fires of the chariots are harnessed... 149 1 2 2 0606a Come to our pressed juice with your bay horses, O Lord of intoxications! 1 2 2 0606c Come to our pressed juice with your bay horses... 150
The desirable oblations have been poured forth, strengthening Indra at the sacrifice;
they flow with might toward the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*).
For I, indeed, have received from my father the wisdom of the Eternal Law (*ṛta*).
I have been born like the sun...
(152) May there be for us, in Indra, rich gifts accompanied by abundant strength, with which we, possessing food, may rejoice. (153)
Soma and Pūṣan have taken notice of all well-established dwellings; they are established as charioteers among the gods.
Sing forth to Indra so that he may drink of your pressed juice.
[To] Viśvāsah, the performer of a hundred sacrifices, the most generous among the people...
155 Sing forth a gladdening song for Indra, the lord of the bay horses, O friends, for the drinker of Soma. 156
O Indra, we Kaṇvas, seeking you as our friends for that very purpose, praise you with hymns.
Let our songs resound all around the pressed juice for Indra, who delights in exhilaration.
Let the singers praise the Sun.
This Soma of yours, O Indra, has been purified upon the sacred grass; come hither, hasten to it, and drink.
For our protection, we invoke day by day the one who fashions beautiful forms, like a well-milking cow for the milker.
O Bull,
now that the soma is pressed, I pour it out for you to drink.
Satisfy yourself; pervade the intoxication! O Indra, that Soma which has been pressed for you in the cups and in the vats—drink of it, for you are its lord.
In every endeavor, in every contest, we invoke you, the most powerful one, O friends, for Indra’s protection. Come hither;
sit down near him; sing forth to Indra.
O friends, you who bring hymns of praise... for this [Soma] has indeed been pressed with might, O Lord of bounties. Drink of it, O lover of songs!
Great is Indra, and let there be great power for us and for the wielder of the thunderbolt; his might is as vast as the sky in its breadth. O Indra, gather for us a wondrous and food-filled prize!
The great-elephant [Indra] with his right [hand]...
167 Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, as he is known:
to the son of truth, the lord of the virtuous. 168
With what aid will he, the ever-increasing friend, come to us with wondrous help? With what most powerful host?
That conqueror of all, whom you invoke in all songs—him indeed.
I have approached the wondrous Lord of the Assembly, the beloved and desirable friend of Indra, seeking the gift of inspired wisdom for our protection. 171
Those paths of yours that are below heaven, by which you sent forth Vyaśva—
may they and the Bhuvans hear us.
O Śatakratu, bring to us what is auspicious, auspicious food and strength.
O Indra, since you would have mercy upon us... 173 This Soma has been pressed; the Maruts drink of it, as do the self-ruling Aśvins. 174
Moving him about, the active ones wait upon Indra at his birth, winning great heroic power.
O gods, we do not neglect you; we do not weary you.
