This unprecedented Dawn shines forth, the beloved of heaven. I praise you both, O Aśvins, with a lofty hymn.
With the bones of Dadhyañc, Indra, unassailable, struck down the Vṛtras.
He struck down ninety-nine [foes].
(RV 1.33.12) Come, O Indra, exhilarate yourself with the soma-juice at every Soma-pressing;
you are great, providing aid through your inherent power. (RV 1.84.4)
Come then to us, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra; come to our side, great one with your mighty aids.
His vigor flared up when he brought both worlds together.
Indra [spread out] heaven and earth like a hide... This one here is yours; you settle upon him like a pigeon upon its nest.
You surely do not disregard that word.
May the Wind blow healing balm toward us—beneficent and delightful to our heart;
may he prolong our lives. Those whom the wise Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman protect...
No person is harmed by him. Just as of old, grant us wealth in cattle, in horses, and in chariots;
bestow upon us the wide space of the great ones.
O Indra, these spotted cows yield for you clarified butter and the milk-mixture;
they are swelling with the nectar of immortality. Through this prayer for cattle, O you of many names, O much-praised one!
1.2.2.1004c: That which is present in every Soma...
188 1.2.2.1005a: May the purifying Sarasvatī, rich in prizes through her powers, 1.2.2.1005c: who possesses wealth through her wisdom, desire our sacrifice. 189
Who among the daughters of Nahuṣa shall satisfy Indra with this Soma? May he bring wealth to us.
Come hither, O Indra, for we have pressed it for you; drink this Soma!
This is my sacred grass, my seat.
Great shall be the protection of the three—of Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa—who dwell in heaven;
it is invincible.
O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth, O Leader, we belong to one such as you; we are the drivers of your two bay steeds.
The Third Prapāṭhaka. First Half.
Having been poured out, may the Soma juices exhilarate you; bestow bounty, O wielder of the stone!
Strike down those who hate the sacred word.
O lover of hymns, drink our pressed juice; you are anointed by the streams of sweetness.
O Indra, glory is indeed bestowed by you. May Indra ever celebrate your deeds;
now, honoring him, no god has surpassed the heroic Indra.

1.3.1.0104a Let the drops enter into you, as rivers flow into the ocean; 1.3.1.0104c O Indra, nothing surpasses you. 1.3.1.0105a Singers sing loudly to Indra; those who offer hymns praise Indra with their songs.
The voices have sung in praise of Indra.
May Indra grant us nourishment, the wealth of Ṛbhukṣan and Ṛbhu;
may the prize-winner grant us the prize.
Indra indeed shall drive away even great fear;
for he is steadfast and far-seeing.
O lover of songs, these hymns reach you at every pressing.
Like milch-cows lowing for their calf... Now let us invoke Indra and Pūṣan for friendship, for well-being, and for the winning of booty.
O Indra, Vṛtra-slayer, there is nothing higher than you, nothing greater; there is no one at all like you.
[I praise] for you the one who carries men across, the piercer of wealth consisting of cattle.
I have likewise praised [thee]...
O Indra, our songs have been poured forth; they have risen up toward thee, the bull, the lord, with one accord.
Truly, that mortal is well-guided whom the Maruts,
whom Aryaman, and the guileless Mitra protect.
O Indra, whatever has been brought away— whether it be in solid rock, in firm ground, or in a mountain cleft.
Bring then that desirable wealth. I have heard of you as the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, the bold host of the peoples, for the sake of great bounty and prosperity.
O Indra, may we come to you for glory, O Hero, as one worthy of you;
O Śakra, may we approach you with devotion.
[We offer] the parched grain, the groats, the cake, and the hymn of praise.
O Indra, enjoy our [offering] in the morning... With the foam of the waters, O Indra, you struck off the head of Namuci,
when you conquered all rival hosts.

These, O Indra, are your Soma juices—those already pressed and those yet to be pressed; rejoice in them, O Lord of abundant wealth! For you the Somas have been pressed, and the sacred grass is strewn, O Radiant One.
O Indra, have mercy upon your praisers...
O Indra, as those seeking booty [pour out the Soma], pour out for us the most bountiful Śatakratu with the drops of Soma.
Therefore, O Indra, come hither to us with food that brings a hundredfold strength, with food that brings a thousandfold strength.
The slayer of Vṛtra took up his arrow; as soon as he was born, he questioned his mother.
Who are the fierce ones? Who indeed are renowned?
We invoke Bṛhaduktha, whose hand is swift, for our protection—him who accomplishes what is right for our aid.
By a straight path may Varuṇa and Mitra, the wise, lead us, as may Aryaman,
in harmony with the gods. Even from afar, as it were, the ruddy-hued one has shone forth from his dwelling.
He has spread his light in every direction. O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter;
O you of noble wisdom, moisten the regions with honey.
1.3.1.0308a Upward those sons have stretched their songs like goal-posts in the sacrifices, 1.3.1.0308c Like lowing cows, to go on bended knees.
1.3.1.0309a Viṣṇu strode across this [universe]; thrice he planted his step.
His [soma] is gathered in the dust...
222 Pass by the one who is full of wrath; urge on the one who has pressed [the soma]. Drink the pressed juice in his bounty. 223
Indeed, a great word is recited for the wise and mighty god; this truly is his means of increase. And the hymn being recited—does the serpent-like wealth take notice of it?
The *gāyatra* being sung...
Indra, most gladdened by the hymns (*uktha*), is the lord of spoils (*vāja*) and the friend of the pressed juices,
accompanied by his bay steeds (*harivat*).
Come to our pressed juice with your strengths; do not be wroth with us, like a great man with a youthful wife.
O Vasu, when will you desire our hymn? Come down to the dwelling where the doors are open.
1.3.1.0406c: For Vātāpya, [recite] the *Dīrghasūta*.
1.3.1.0407a: O Indra, drink the Soma from the Brahmin’s bounty according to the seasons;
1.3.1.0407c: this friendship of yours is invincible. 228–229.
O Indra, lover of songs, we indeed belong to you as your praisers; O drinker of Soma, quicken us.
O Indra, bestow manly strength upon us in whatever battles there may be.
Satrājit [possesses] fierce manly power... Thus indeed you are one who seeks heroes, thus a hero, and thus steadfast;
thus indeed is your mind to be won over.
We cry out to you, O Hero, like unmilked cows, to you,
the lord of this moving world, the beholder of heaven, the lord, O Indra, of all that stands still. For we, the singers, invoke you alone for the winning of booty.
O Indra, lord of the virtuous, men call upon you in battles against the Vṛtras;

they call upon you in the races for the prize of heaven. Sing forth your praise to Indra, the giver of great wealth, as he is known to be—he who, as Maghavan, possessor of many riches, bestows gifts upon his singers as if by the thousands.
We praise with songs that Indra for you— the wondrous one who overcomes enemies, who rejoices in the exhilarating food— just as cows low toward their calf in the stalls.
With our hymns, we urgently invoke for your aid Indra, the finder of wealth.
Singing loudly at the sacrifice where the Soma has been pressed, I call upon him as a craftsman calls for his prize.
With the goddess Purandhi as my companion, he indeed strives to win the prize.
Like a carpenter fashions a well-wrought felly, I bend Indra—the one invoked by many—toward me with my song.
Drink of the pressed juice, O Indra; exhilarate yourself with our soma mixed with milk.
Be our kinsman at the communal feast for our prosperity; may your insights protect us.
For you indeed come to the one who strives, finding fortune for the sake of bestowing wealth.
Pour forth for us, O Maghavan, for the winning of cattle; O Indra, pour forth for the winning of horses.
For neither the last nor Vasiṣṭha among you has ever disregarded us.
O Maruts, may all of you who desire it drink today at our pressed soma.
1.3.1.0510a Do not praise anything else at all; O friends, do not suffer harm.
1.3.1.0510c Praise only Indra, the bull, when the soma is pressed; repeatedly recite hymns of praise.
The Third Chapter. Second Half.
No one who has performed the ever-increasing rite is harmed by his action—
not Indra, who is praised by all, skillful, unassailable, and bold in his might, as if through sacrifices.
He who, even without a binding, pierces through the joints before they are joined.
Maghavan, the lord of many riches, is the restorer of alliances; he repairs again what has been shattered.
(244) May a thousand and a hundred steeds, yoked to thy golden chariot—bay horses with long manes, harnessed by prayer—bring thee hither, O Indra, for the drinking of Soma. (245)
Come, O Indra, with your pleasant, peacock-haired bay horses!
Let no snarers restrain you; pass them by like a desert. You indeed, O most powerful god, shall praise the mortal man.
O Maghavan, there is no one other than you who shows mercy; O Indra, I speak these words to you.
You, O Indra, are glorious, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, the lord of power.
You alone slay the irresistible Vṛtras, you who are unassailable, the sustainer of the people.
Indra for the worship of the gods; Indra as the sacrifice proceeds;
Indra we, the seekers of booty, invoke at the encounter; Indra for the winning of wealth.
O Lord of abundant wealth, may these songs of mine increase thee.
Pure and wise, with the color of fire, they have been praised with hymns of praise. These most honey-sweet songs and chants rise up;
like chariots seeking booty, they are ever-conquering winners of wealth, possessing inexhaustible aid and striving for victory.
Just as a thirsty buffalo goes to a water-hole in the desert, come quickly to us at the beginning and at the end of our journey; drink well among the Kaṇvas.
O Indra, Lord of Power, be gracious with all your aids.
For we follow you, O hero, the glorious finder of wealth,

like a lord of fortune. O Indra, those enjoyments which you, the possessor of light, brought from the Asuras— O Maghavan, increase the singer of this hymn and those who have spread the sacrificial grass for you.

O you who dwell in Truth, sing a helpful song for Mitra, a pleasing word for Aryaman, and a laud for Varuṇa, for their protection, among these kings. O Indra, toward you the Āyus have turned with hymns for the first draught.
The *Ṛbhus*, acting in unison, raised their voices together; the *Rudras* sang praise to the Ancient One.
O Maruts, offer a prayer to your great Indra!
Let the Vṛtra-slayer, the Lord of a hundred powers, slay Vṛtra with his hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
Sing forth, O Maruts, a great song for Indra, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra,
by whom the upholders of Ṛta generated light— the god who is ever-watchful for the sake of the gods. O Indra, bring us wisdom, as a father brings it to his sons.
O much-invoked one, may we learn this path of yours; living, may we attain the light.
O Indra, do not cast us away; be with us at our common feast.
You alone are our protection, you alone are our kinship; O Indra, do not cast us away.
O Vṛtra-slayer, we who have pressed the Soma and trimmed the sacred grass sit around you as your praisers at the outpourings of the filter, like waters.
O Indra, whatever strength and manly valor exists among the Nahuṣa tribes and among the peoples— [that is yours].
Or rather, bring hither the glory of the five peoples and all manly powers together.
Truly, you are indeed a bull; with the impulse of a bull, be our protector.
For you, O fierce one, are heard of as a bull in the distance, and as a bull you are renowned nearby.
Whether you are in the distance, O Śakra, or nearby, O slayer of Vṛtra— therefore the presser of Soma,
with longing songs, seeks to win you, O Indra, with his long-maned hymns.
Sing forth with your voice to the hero for the exhilaration of the soma-juice, to the great and wise one.
O Indra, by name, the famous and powerful one, according as the word [describes you]...
(265) O Indra, grant for our well-being a triple-layered refuge, a triple-fortified shelter. Bestow protection upon the liberal patrons and upon me; ward off the missile from them. (266)
Like people rising toward the sun, may all partake of Indra’s bounty. Having been born with power over all generations, we look forward to our allotted share as our portion.
O immortal one, no mortal shall attain that nourishment, O long-lived one.
Even as Etaśa yoked his coursers, so Indra yoked his two bay steeds.
O Vṛtra-slayer, O most mighty one, O you who are praised in hymns, adorn Indra for us in all battles—him who is to be invoked—with our prayers and libations. 268–269.
O Indra, yours is the lowest wealth; you nourish the middlemost;
you truly rule over all that is highest. No one holds you back when it comes to cattle. Where are you going? Where are you? For your mind is indeed in many places.
O warrior, shaker of the rattle, breaker of forts, you are exhilarated; the *gāyatrī* hymns have been sung forth to you.
We ourselves have indeed nourished this wielder of the thunderbolt here;
bring him today at this libation the pressed soma. Now, pay homage to the one who is renowned.
He who is the king of the peoples, who advances with his chariots irresistible,
the overcomer of all hostile armies— he whom I praise as the supreme slayer of Vṛtra.
O Indra, from whatever we fear, grant us freedom from that fear.
O Maghavan, grant us this for your aid; strike away our enemies and our adversaries.
O Vāstoṣpati, you are the firm pillar, the constant refuge of those who offer Soma. Indra, the breaker of many fortresses, is the friend of the sages.
Great indeed you are, O Sūrya; great indeed you are, O Āditya.
Your greatness, being so vast, is most worthy of praise; by your majesty, O God, you are great.
When your friend, O Indra, is possessed of horses, a chariot, beautiful form, and cattle—*276*—he is truly well-favored.
He is ever accompanied by a vigorous age that bestows prosperity; with his radiant [splendor], he approaches the assembly hall.
O Indra, even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths belonging to you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, neither the thousand suns nor the two worlds could equal you at your birth.
O Indra, whether you are invoked by men in the east, the west, the north, or the south—being impelled by many heroes, you belong to the Anu people; O bold one, you belong to Turvaśa.
O Indra, what mortal dares to oppose you, the Vasu?
For faith, O Maghavan, on the decisive day, like a prize-winning steed, seeks to win the prize for you.
O Indra and Agni, this [cow] has come first, having gone before those that have feet.
Having left her head behind, she bleats with her tongue; she has stepped down thirty paces.
O Indra, come nearer with your aids that are well-intended; come with most auspicious protections, O most auspicious one; come with sleep-inducing powers, O you who bring sleep.
From here, for your sake, [I call] the ageless one, the hurler who is not hurled.
The swift victor, the striker, the best of charioteers, the unsubdued one who increased for Tugriya...
O you who are invoked by the priests, let them not detain you far from us; whether you come to our common feast from afar, or being already here, listen to us.
Press out the Soma for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the drinker of Soma. Cook the cooked offerings for his protection; for he who bestows gifts brings joy to the one who gives.
We invoke that Indra, the all-conquering one who moves among the people.
O you of many powers, O lord of great manly might, be present in our battles for our prosperity.
(1.3.2.1004c) O you two possessors of power, by your mighty deeds, grant us your favor day and night. May your bounty never fail us; may your bounty never fail us at any time. (1.3.2.1005a-c)
Whenever a mortal singer may praise the Bountiful One,
let him then awaken Varuṇa with inspired song— the upholder of those who follow different laws.
O Medhyātithi, protect the cattle in the exhilaration of the Soma-juice for Indra.
He who is joined with two bay steeds, he who is golden, Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is golden. May Indra hear both [of us] here; may he turn this speech toward himself.
May the most powerful Maghavan come with his focused mind for the drinking of the Soma.
Even for a great price, O wielder of the stone, you are not given away;
not for a thousand, nor for ten thousand, O wielder of the thunderbolt, nor for a hundred, O you whose wealth consists of hundreds.
O Indra, you are better to me than my father and even than my brother who does not enjoy [my wealth].
And you two, O Vasus, delight my mother with your common wealth for the sake of prosperity.
[End of] the Fourth Prapāṭhaka. First Half.
1.4.1. These Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for Indra.
Come with your two bay horses, O wielder of the thunderbolt, to this dwelling for exhilaration and to drink.
O Indra, these Somas have been prepared for your exhilaration; they have shone forth as songs of praise. Having drunk of the sweetness, listen to our hymns and grant them to us, O lover of song!

I call today upon you, Indra, the one who stirs the *gāyatrī* hymn, the milch-cow who yields nectar, the well-milking cow, the other [source] of nourishment, the wide-streaming one who bestows all things. O Indra,
the great and solid mountains do not obstruct you.
Whatever wealth you bestow upon one who praises you like me, no one shall diminish that of yours. Who knows him as he drinks at the pressed juice? What age has he assumed?
He is this very one who, exhilarated by the soma-plant, shatters the fortresses with his might, O fair-cheeked one.
O Indra, cast down from his seat the lawless one whom you punish;
O Maghavan, increase our much-desired stalk of Soma for the sake of great wealth.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, Parjanya, and Brahmaṇaspati [bless] our divine speech.
May Aditi protect us with her sons and brothers; may our invincible word be a means of deliverance.
(299) And when will you not be barren, O Indra? Do you never fail the donor? O Maghavan, ever more and more is the gift of you, the god, bestowed. (300)
Harness, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, your two bay steeds from afar;
come hither, O Maghavan, for the drinking of the Soma—come, O fierce one, with the Ṛṣis.
For yesterday the zealous men made you swell, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
O Indra, you who are borne by hymns of praise, hear us here; come to our dwelling place.
The daughter of Heaven has been seen approaching, shining forth. The noble one uncovers the waters with her eye; she dispels the darkness and creates light.
These very morning sacrifices, O Aśvins, call upon you at dawn.
I here invoke you both for protection, O lords of power, for you go to every clan. Where are you? What mortal, O Aśvins, is performing fervent heat (penance) for you, O gods?
Striking with the stone and crushing the stalks, he has pressed [the juice] for you thus; so now, O Aśvins...
This most honeyed Soma has been pressed for you at the morning sacrifices.
Drink it, O Aśvins, that which was prepared over the past day; bestow treasures upon the donor.
1.4.1.0205a Always entreating you with the flowing stream of Soma, I, the archer, have provoked you at the libations like a wild beast; for who would not entreat one who is powerful?
307 1.4.1.0206a O Adhvaryu, cause the Soma to flow; Indra thirsts for it.
1.4.1.0206c Surely now he has yoked his two bay steeds with the bull [Indra]; the slayer of Vṛtra has arrived.
308 1.4.1.0207a O Bṛhaddiva, bring that wealth from the younger man to the elder.
1.4.1.0207c For you, O Maghavan, have become one who possesses abundant wealth; and in every battle, you are to be invoked. 309

O Indra, if I were the lord of as much wealth as you possess, I would surely provide for my singer, O Dispenser of Riches; I would not leave him to misery. You, O Indra, prevail over all rival hosts in the battles of onset.

You are the slayer of the reviler, the progenitor, the overcomer of Vṛtra; do you overcome those who seek to overcome us. He who by his might has cast down the seat of heaven—O Indra, the earthly realm did not contain you; you have grown beyond all.
The god-impelling juice has been pressed; Indra has taken pleasure in it from his very birth.
We awaken you, O Lord of the bay horses, with sacrifices; awaken our hymn of praise in the exhilaration of the soma-juice.
A seat has been prepared for you, O Indra, in the dwelling; come to it, O much-invoked one, with your men.
Just as you were our protector and increaser, bestowing riches and rejoicing in the Soma juices—
You shattered the waters, you released the channels, and you set free the obstructed floods. O Indra, when you split the great mountain and let forth the streams, you struck down the Dānavas.
Having pressed the Soma, O Indra, we praise you, desiring to win booty, O you of many heroic deeds. Bring us prosperity, that which we may conquer by ourselves, by our lineage, and by your aid.
We have grasped your right hand, O Indra, seeking wealth, O Lord of treasures.
For we know you, O Hero, as the lord of cattle; grant us wonderful, bull-like wealth.

(317) Men invoke Indra in the contest for the prize, when they harness those thoughts that lead to the further shore. O Hero, in the winning of men and in the desire for glory, grant us our share in the cow-stall. (318)
The Suparṇas, the Priyamedha seers, have approached Indra with their supplication.

Dispel the darkness, fill our eyes with light, and release us like those bound in a snare. When they beheld you with longing hearts as you flew toward the firmament like a Suparṇa, they gazed upon you.
The golden-winged messenger of Varuṇa, the bird hurrying to the abode of Yama...
Brahman, first born in the east, Vena revealed from the radiant horizon;
he disclosed its highest stations, the foundations of the world, and the source of both the existent and the non-existent.

For him, the great hero, the powerful and swift one, they have fashioned most unprecedented and most abundant words— most auspicious for this exuberant wielder of the thunderbolt, for this steadfast one.
The dark drop descended upon the Aṃśumatī river as it flowed away, accompanied by ten thousand [followers].
Indra, by his power, blew away the snorting cloud that was turning back; he, the manly-minded one, cast down those who were weak.
Fleeing from the snort of Vṛtra, all the gods who were your friends abandoned you.
O Indra, let there be friendship between you and the Maruts; then you shall conquer all these hostile armies.
The gray-haired one has swallowed the young moon as he sped through the assembly of the many.
Behold the poetic power of the god in its greatness: he who was alive yesterday has died today.
At your very birth, O Indra, you became the enemy to those seven who had no enemies.

In the hidden depths you found heaven and earth; you bestowed joy upon the far-reaching worlds. Like a pillar, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you are sharp-edged, many-sustaining, a bull of steadfast power.
You make the hostile ones flee; desiring to serve, O Indra, I praise you, the celestial slayer of Vṛtra.
Bring forth your song to the great one, the increaser of greatness, the wise one; offer up your devotion. Go forth to the many tribes, O filler of the people!
We invoke for our good fortune the bounteous Indra, the most heroic, in this battle for the winning of booty.
Hear him, the fierce one, for our protection in battles; he who slays the Vṛtras and wins riches.
329 The sacred hymns have risen up toward Indra, O Vasiṣṭha, to magnify him in the assembly.
He who has spread himself far with his glory—hears the words of one such as me. 330
The wheel of his which is set within the waters—may he grant us that honey-sweet [portion] from it.
That udder of the earth which is poured out, you placed the milk within the cows and the plants.
That very vigorous one, impelled by the gods, the mighty conqueror who overcomes chariots—him indeed [I praise].
For our well-being, let us here invoke Tārkṣya, the unassailable, the conqueror of armies, the swift one.
I invoke Indra, the protector; I invoke Indra, the helper; at every call, I invoke the hero Indra, who is easily invoked.
Now I call upon Śakra, Indra who is invoked by many; may Maghavan Indra partake of this oblation.
Let us worship Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his right hand, the charioteer of the bay steeds that move in various directions.
Shaking his beard, he stands tall; terrifying with his armies, he prevails through his bounty.
We invoke Indra—the ever-conquering, bold, and impetuous one, the great and boundless bull, wielder of the excellent thunderbolt.

He who is the slayer of Vṛtra and the winner of booty, the Maghavan who bestows riches and is most bountiful— may we, protected by you, O Indra of virile mind, overcome through battle or through power that mortal who, seeking to harm us, assails us with his host or with his haste. 335–336.
He whom the people, contending with their enemies, invoke; whom those striving for speed invoke when their horses are yoked;
whom they call upon in the battle for heroes, whom they call upon at the onset of the waters, and whom the sages seek for booty—that is Indra.
O Indra and Parvata, bring hither on your great chariot desirable refreshments accompanied by brave sons.
O Gods, partake of the oblations at the sacrifices; may you both grow strong, rejoicing in our songs and in the sacrificial food.

For Indra, he has sent forth songs with unrestrained flow, as he drove the waters from the depths of the ocean—that one who, by his powers, propped apart the earth and the sky on all sides, as if with two wheels held by an axle.
May your friends turn you toward them with their friendship; may you pass even across many seas.
May the wise one establish the grandson of the father in this dwelling, shining forth for a longer duration. Who today yokes to the pole of Order the vigorous, impetuous, and ill-disposed oxen?
Near them are the water-bearers, the sources of bliss; he who provides for their maintenance shall live.
(End of the fourth section. Second Half. 1.4.2. They sing to you, O singers of the *gāyatrī*; those who recite the *ṛk* verses praise the *ṛk*.
The Brahmins have raised you up, O Śatakratu, like a sacrificial post.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean,
the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.

O Indra, drink this pressed juice, the supreme, immortal exhilaration. The streams of the bright [Soma] have flowed toward you at the seat of the Cosmic Order (Ṛta). O Indra, wielder of the stone, whatever wonderful thing is not here that can be given by you—[grant it to me].
O possessor of all wealth, bring us prosperity with both your hands;
hear the call of Tiraścī, O Indra, who honors you.
Fill us with riches consisting of brave sons and cattle; for you are great.
The Soma has been pressed for you, O Indra; come, most powerful and bold one!
May vital power fill you, as the sun fills the mid-air with its rays. Come, O Indra, with your bay steeds to the beautiful hymn of Kaṇva.
From that heaven, you who rule over heaven, you who go to heaven, O you whose wealth is light...
(348) Like a charioteer, songs have mounted toward you when the juices are pressed, O lover of song. They have cried out to you in unison, as milch-cows low toward their calf. (349)
Come now, let us praise Indra, the pure one, with a pure *sāman*;
may he, who has grown strong through pure hymns (*uktha*), be exhilarated by the pure invocations.
He who is the wealthiest of you all, the most resplendent in splendors—
O Indra, Lord of the *svadhā*, this pressed Soma is your exhilarating drink. Bring all [offerings] to him who desires to drink, to the one who knows all things,
to the one who comes readily and moves swiftly, whose path is never behind, O men!
Bring hither for us that which lies in every nest, the great one dwelling in the depths, the great one dwelling in the ancient places.
You have struck down the fierce word. We turn you hither like a chariot for our protection and for our favor.
Indra, the most powerful lord of the virtuous, who performs great deeds, overcomes distress, and endures in battle—
him, the ancient one, the beloved, he has anointed with holy rites,
he through whose doors Manu the father anointed his prayers among the gods.
When the swift, radiant steeds carry [you] upon the chariots,
drinking the intoxicating honey-sweet mead, there they win for themselves glorious fame.
I praise that lord of power for you, who is never to be struck down.
Indra, the all-conquering hero, most powerful, the knower of all; ...
I have offered praise to Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, the spirited steed. May he make our mouths fragrant; may he prolong our lives.
The breaker of forts, the youth, the sage of immeasurable power was born;
Indra, the sustainer of every deed, the wielder of the thunderbolt, praised by many.
Sing forth the *triṣṭubh* hymn, a nourishing offering, for the hero-souled Indu.
With wisdom and with inspired thought, he seeks to win you for the acquisition of the sacrifice.
360 Of Kaśyapa, who has found the light of heaven, they speak of the two as "the yoked pair.
361 The wise, having discerned their all-encompassing vow and the sacrifice, [worship them]. 361
Sing, O men, sing forth with praise! O Priyamedhas, sing! Let the sons also sing; yea, sing to the bold Puramit!
A hymn is to be recited for Indra, a strengthening song for the one who repels many foes.
May Śakra rejoice in our sons and in our friendship, as he does now.
I invoke with my movements the Lord of Wealth, Viśvānara, who possesses unbending power, for the sake of the protection of the people and of chariots.
O hero of heaven, he who, through the prayer of a mortal man who exerts himself, wins your favor—he, by the aid of the great heaven, crosses over his enemies as if over distress.
O Indra, lord of a hundred powers, your wealth is vast; your gift is vast.
Then, O you who belong to all people, O bounteous giver, bestow glory upon us. Even the winged birds, the bipeds, and the quadrupeds, O radiant one,
have awakened at your coming, O Dawn, following their appointed seasons from the very ends of heaven.
O you who are these gods in the midst of the luminous realm of heaven— what is your *ṛta*, what is your *amṛta*, and what is your ancient oblation?
We worship the *ṛc* and the *sāman*, by which they perform their sacred rites.
May they two shine forth in the assembly; may they carry the sacrifice to the gods.
The men, acting in concert, have fashioned Indra for sovereignty, him who overcomes all hostile armies.
For the sake of wisdom, for the sake of choice stability, they have produced the wide-reaching, fierce, most powerful, impetuous, and swift one.
I entrust myself to your first wrathful power, when you struck down the Dasyu, the man-slayer, and set the waters free.
When both world-halves ran after you, O wielder of the stone, even the earth trembled before your impetuous might.
All gather together through his strength—he who alone has become the lord of heaven and the guest of men.
He, the ancient one, seeks to win the new; he alone has turned toward him along the paths.
O Indra, much-praised Lord of abundant wealth, we here are yours—we who move about having taken hold of you.
For there is none other than you, O lover of songs, who can sustain our hymns, just as the two worlds sustain all things. Accept this our speech with favor.
The lofty hymns have sung aloud to Indra, the sustainer of the people, the Maghavan worthy of praise;
to him who is magnified by well-fashioned songs, the immortal one who is celebrated day by day, the one invoked by many.
Toward you, O Indra, all our yearning thoughts, longing for heaven, have sung in unison.
They embrace him as wives embrace a husband, like a pure young man for the sake of aid—the bountiful Maghavan.
375 Exhilarate with songs that ram, Indra, who is invoked by many and worthy of praise, the ocean of wealth.
376 Praise the most generous sage, whose human-like bounty spreads abroad like the heavens, so that he may grant us enjoyment. 376
That ram, the finder of light, whom a hundred well-being-bestowing ones accompany together—
I would turn that chariot, Indra, who speeds to the invocation like a prize-winning steed, toward us for protection with my well-fashioned hymns.
The two worlds, rich in ghee, the overlords of all beings, wide and broad, yielding honey and beautifully adorned.
Heaven and earth are held apart by the law of Varuṇa; they are ageless and possess abundant seed.
Since you, O Indra, have filled both worlds like the dawn, we recognize you as the great sovereign of the mighty ones and the ruler of all people.

The goddess, the mother, gave birth; the auspicious one, the mother, gave birth. Sing forth a word full of nourishment for the gladdening one, who with Ṛjiśvan struck down those whose wombs were black.
Seeking aid, we would invoke for friendship the bull-like one who wields the thunderbolt in his right hand, accompanied by the Maruts.

O Indra, when the Soma juices have been pressed, you purify your praiseworthy power of will; for he is great through his increasing skill and wisdom. Sing forth unto him, the one invoked by many, the one praised by many.
1.4.2.1002c With songs of praise, bring hither Indra, the powerful one. ...

382 1.4.2.1003a We celebrate that exhilarating draught of yours, the bull-like, victorious one among the nourishments; 1.4.2.1003c O wielder of the stone, we praise him who creates wide space and possesses the glory of the tawny steeds. 383
Whether you, O Indra, rejoice in Soma with Viṣṇu, or with Trita Āptya,
or whether you delight among the Maruts with the drops—
come hither, O Adhvaryu, and pour out the most intoxicating of the sweet juices.
For thus is the hero, ever-increasing, praised.
Pour out the soma-juice for Indra; let him drink the honeyed mead. By his greatness, he impels forth bounteous gifts.
Come now, O friends, let us praise Indra, the hero worthy of hymns, he who alone surpasses all the peoples. Sing forth a lofty *sāman* for Indra, the inspired sage, the great one.
To the one made by Brahmā, the wise, the one worthy of praise... (388) He alone bestows wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations;
the sovereign, the unopposed Indra—verily so! (389)
O friends, we instruct a sacred prayer for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
I praise you well for him who is most heroic and bold.
Fifth Prapāṭhaka, First Half.
I sing this, O Indra, of your preeminent power for the assembly of the gods—
that you, O Lord of Might, slay Vṛtra with your strength. It was in your exhilaration that you delivered Śambara to Divodāsa.
This is that Soma pressed for you, O Indra; drink it!
Come to us, O Indra, beloved one, ever-conquering, unconcealable, broad on every side like a mountain, the lord of heaven.
O Indra, that exhilaration which is the greatest drinker of Soma, O most powerful one, which is conscious—that by which you strike down the devourers, for that we pray.
For our offspring, for our progeny, grant us that very thing: a longer life to live.
O Ādityas,

you who are equal in greatness, bring about [this]! For you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, know how to avoid the snares of Destruction (Nirṛti) day after day, like one who purifies himself from footprints.
Drive away disease, drive away the sting, drive away ill-will;
O Ādityas, keep us far from distress.
Drink the soma, O Indra; let that which the stone has pressed for you exhilarate you, O Lord of the Tawny Steeds.
Well-restrained by the arms of Sotu, he is not like a horse [held by the reins]. O Indra, you are from of old, by birth, without a rival, without kin, and without a friend;
yet in battle, you desire companionship.
I praise for you that Indra, the friend, for protection—he who brought this wealth here from of old. O friends, come hither;
do not fail us! O you who are ever-faring, do not stay away, O you of one mind!
Even that which is firm, they cause to tremble.
Come hither for this Soma-juice, O Lord of Horses, Lord of Cattle, Lord of Fields! Drink the Soma, O Lord of Soma!
O Bull, with you as our ally, may we indeed speak back to the one who snorts in defiance at the gathering of the cattle-owning folk.
For even the cows are of one mind; O Maruts, you are kinsmen by common descent.
They lick one another's peaks...
O Indra, bring to us strength and manly valor, O Lord of a hundred powers, O far-seeing one; bring a hero who conquers in battle.
Now, O Indra, lover of songs, we approach you with longing; we have come together like waters flowing upward.
Sitting there like birds, they [revel] in the exhilarating, speech-inspiring honey-mixture mixed with milk.
We cry out to you, O Indra:
"Be mindful of us! We, seeking your aid, call upon you, the matchless one—like those carrying a heavy burden—we invoke you, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the wondrous one.
From this very source, from the center of the sweet mead, the tawny cows drink;
they who, moving together with the bull Indra, rejoice in splendor—being excellent, they follow their own sovereignty.
For thus indeed has Soma, the exhilarating one, performed the strengthening prayer.
O most powerful wielder of the thunderbolt, by your might you have driven the serpent from the earth;

we sing praises after [the pattern of] your self-rule. Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been strengthened by men for exhilaration and for power. Him we invoke for aid in great battles and in small; may he further us in the contests for booty.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, O thunderbolt-wielder, yours alone is this unyielding heroic power.
When you slew that guileful beast with your own wondrous might, you celebrated your own sovereign dominion.
Go forth! Attack! Be bold! Your thunderbolt shall not be held back.
O Indra, for yours is manly strength and power; slay Vṛtra, win the waters, and sing in praise of your own sovereignty.

When battles arise and wealth is set before the bold, yoke your two bay steeds that distill exhilaration. Whom will you slay? To whom will you grant riches? O Indra, place us among those who possess wealth.
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; the dear ones have shaken themselves free.
The self-luminous sages have offered praise with their newest hymn: "Now, O Indra, yoke your two bay steeds.
Listen well to our songs, O Maghavan; do not treat us like strangers.
When will you grant us wealth that brings true prosperity? O Indra, yoke now your two bay steeds for our purpose!
The moon moves within the waters; the fair-winged bird flies in the sky.
O lightnings with golden rims, you do not find my footstep; O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
The singer, O Aśvins, adorns with hymns your most beloved, manly chariot that carries wealth; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O Agni, may we kindle you—the radiant, undecaying god.
Your most excellent battle-skill shall shine forth; O kindled one, you illuminate the heavens. Bring nourishment to those who praise you.

With our own well-fashioned hymns, we choose you as the Hotṛ priest—sharp and with purifying luster—at the sacrifices where the sacred grass is strewn. In your exhilaration, you desire to speak aloud.
O Uṣas, radiant as the sun, awaken us today for the sake of wealth,
just as you have awakened us before for Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born one, rich in horses and noble gifts!
Send forth to us a blessed mind, as well as skill and wisdom.
Then, in your friendship with the soma-juice, in the exhilaration of the draught, you take delight like cattle in a pasture—you are being celebrated.
Great by his mental power, according to his own nature, the terrible one has turned toward his might.
Sublime in splendor, the fair-cheeked, tawny-hued god has taken the iron thunderbolt in his two hands.
May he indeed mount that powerful, cattle-finding chariot—he, O Indra, who has set his mind upon the full vessel of the *hariyojana* offering; now, O Indra, yoke your two bay steeds!
I think of that Agni who is the wealthy one, toward whom the milch-cows go.
Eight swift coursers, eight constant stallions— bring nourishment to those who praise you! O gods, neither distress nor misfortune overtakes that mortal whom Aryaman,
Mitra, and Varuṇa lead together in harmony across his enemies.
Flow forth, O Soma, as a sweet draught for Indra, for Mitra, for Pūṣan, and for Bhaga.
Flow forth indeed for the winning of booty; as one who overcomes obstacles, flow around us. To cross over our enemies, you hasten like a debt-collector.
Flow on, O Soma, as a great ocean, the father of the gods, toward all abodes.
Flow on, O Soma, for great skill, like a washed horse, a prize-winner, for the sake of wealth.
The lovely drop has flowed for exhilaration, the sage in the lap of the waters, for good fortune.
For we rejoice in you, O Soma, when you are pressed, for the sake of great sovereignty over the assembly.
O Pavamāna, you plunge forward toward the spoils of war. Who are these men, the companions of Rudra, the youths with noble horses, who are clearly distinguished?
O Agni, may we today succeed for you with our hymns—as one would with a horse—with a thought that is auspicious and touches the heart;
may we prosper through our offerings. O noble ones, the prize-seekers have come forth toward the prize, toward the impulse of the god Savitṛ.
O swift steeds, win the heavens... 435.
Flow on, O Soma, radiant, with a fine stream, great and following the ancient succession of the sheep’s wool. 436.
The Fifth Chapter. Second Half.
O you who give from every side, bring to us from every side that which we seek from you, O most powerful one!
(437) This is the priest who is timely; he is celebrated by the name Indra, and I sing his praise.
(438) The priests, magnifying Indra with hymns, strengthened him for the slaying of Ahi. (439)

The Anus have fashioned a chariot for your horse; Tvaṣṭṛ, O much-invoked one, has fashioned the radiant thunderbolt. Like those who possess wealth, they promote the auspicious step and bounty; he who lacks self-restraint does not fulfill his desire, nor does he attain riches. Always are the cows pure and all-sustaining; always are the gods stainless.
Come hither with the wood; the cows follow the path with their full udders.
Dwellers near the honey-sweet food, may we prosper; O Indra, we meditate upon your wealth.
The Maruts, singers of beautiful songs, sing their hymn of praise; that famous youth, Indra, utters his roar.
Sing forth a song for Indra, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, the sage, whom he shall delight.
Agni has become perceptive, the wise bearer of oblations, whose chariot is auspicious.
O Agni, be our closest kin, our protector, our gracious guardian.
Like Bhaga, Agni is wondrous; he bestows treasure upon the great ones.
Whether from afar or indeed right here, let there now be a loud shout of praise for all.
Dawn, most excellent sister, rolls back the path by virtue of her noble birth.
May we, together with Indra and all the gods, establish these worlds for ourselves. O Indra, let your gifts flow forth like streams along the paths.
Through this [sacrifice], may we win the strength ordained by the gods; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
Through *ūrj* (nourishment), Mitra and Varuṇa cause the sacrificial offerings (*iḍā*) to swell; O Indra, make our food (*iṣ*) abundant.
Indra rules over all.
At the Trikadruka rites, the mighty bull, possessing great strength, drank his fill of the barley-mixed Soma pressed by Viṣṇu, according to his desire.
He has exhilarated him for the performance of great deeds—the great and wide one; truly, the divine drop (indu) has accompanied the divine Indra, the true one with the true one.
This [Soma], the thousandfold thinker, is the vision of the seers, the thought, the light, the upholder of the law.
The ruddy sun (bradhna) has sent forth the united dawns, the faultless ones, of one mind, full of spirit at their station, intent upon the cow.

O Indra, come to us from afar like a lord of the people to the assemblies, like a king, a lord of the people, shooting his arrows. We invoke you while offering oblations at the pressed juices, as sons call upon a father for the winning of booty—upon you, the most bountiful, for the winning of booty.
I repeatedly call upon that Indra, the munificent and fierce one, who ever bestows many glories, being himself unassailable.
Most bountiful and worthy of sacrifice, may he turn toward us through our hymns; may the wielder of the thunderbolt make all paths easy for our wealth.
May there be a hearing! With my prayer, I place Agni at the forefront. Now we choose that divine host; we choose Indra and Vāyu.
For when they were joined together for Vivasvat, as a bond for a new [sacrifice]—
Now indeed our prayers go forth toward the gods like inspired thoughts; our prayers go forth toward the gods.
Let your hymns go forth to the great Viṣṇu, who is accompanied by the Maruts—the mountain-born songs, O Evayāmarut!
Let them go forth to the host that is worthy of sacrifice, the joyous, the powerful, the one whose gifts are to be celebrated, the one of roaring laws, for the sake of strength.
With this ruddy luster, being purified, he overcomes all hostilities with his companions, as the sun does with his companions.
The stream of the back shines forth as he is purified, the ruddy, golden-hued one.
When you encompass all forms with the singers, with the seven-mouthed singers.

I praise that god Savitar between the two worlds, the one of seer-like insight, whose impulse is true, who bestows treasures—the beloved thought. Whose lofty splendor has shone forth at his impelling; the golden-handed one of good wisdom has measured out the light with his form.
I honor Agni as the Hotṛ-priest, the bountiful, the son of strength, Jātavedas, like a sage, like Jātavedas.
The god whose sacrifice is well-performed, with his upward-reaching form turned toward the gods,

follows the radiant glow of clarified butter as he is offered the melted fat, possessing bright luster. O dancer, O Indra, that heroic deed of yours— the first and ancient work worthy of proclamation in heaven— was performed by you for the waters.

He who by the power of the god sent forth the living breath and released the waters—he has become superior to every god by his might. May he of a hundred powers find us strength; may he find food for us.
Thus ends the Indra section, the *kāṇḍa*.
O Pāvamāna,
your birth from the pressed soma-juice is high; established in heaven,
it is received upon the earth— terrible protection and great renown.
Flow on with your sweetest, most intoxicating stream, O Soma,
pressed for Indra to drink.
Flow as a bull with your stream, you who exhilarate the Maruts.
Bestowing all things by his might... With that exhilarating juice of yours which is most excellent, flow clear with your essence, O god-favored one, slayer of the wicked.
Three voices rise up; the cows low as milch-kine;
the tawny one goes forth bellowing.
O Indu, flow most sweetly for Indra accompanied by the Maruts.
To sit upon the womb of the sun...
472 This shoot, the skillful one dwelling on the mountain, has been pressed in the waters for intoxication; like a hawk, it has settled in its womb. 473
Flow on, O tawny one, as the accomplisher of skill, for the gods to drink;
flow as a gladdening draught for the Maruts and for Vāyu. Being pressed and dwelling upon the mountains, Soma has flowed through the filter.
In all ways you are among the exhilarating drinks...
475 The sage of heaven, the friend of the two daughters, goes toward the nourishments with his own resonant songs; he whose wisdom is that of a seer proceeds [there]. 476
The Soma drops, distilling exhilaration, have been pressed for our patrons' glory;
they have stepped forth into the assembly hall. The wise Soma drops, like surging waves, lead the waters forward.
Like buffaloes [entering] the forests...
Flow clear, O Indu, as the pressed bull; make us glorious among the people.
Strike away all our enemies.
For you are a bull by your radiance; we invoke you, the brilliant one, O Pavamāna, the beholder of heaven.
Indu, the conscious and beloved thought of the sages, has flowed forth.
Like a charioteer, he has let loose the horse. The Soma juices, seeking cattle and seeking horses, have been poured forth; bright and swift, they seek heroes.
Flow on, O God, for the sake of long life; let your exhilaration go to Indra.
Ascend to Vāyu according to the cosmic law. Flowing clear, Pavamāna has generated from heaven a wondrous sound like thunder.
The great Vaiśvānara light...
The pressed Soma drops, for exhilaration, flow forth with power and song;
they stream with a current of honeyed sweetness.
The sage, resting upon the wave of the ocean, has breathed forth [the hymn],
bearing the seer who is desired by many.
Sixth Prapāṭhaka, First Half.
The gods have come to the pressed juice, the son of the waters, adorned with milk, the breaker of obstacles. Purifying himself, the far-seeing one has stepped upon all adversaries.
They adorn the sage with their prayers.
488 Flowing toward all splendors, the pressed juice enters the jar; Indu is prepared for Indra. 489
Like a chariot-horse, the pressed juice has been released into the two bowls; like a prize-winning steed, it has stepped down upon the goal.
When, like restless bulls, the brilliant and tireless ones have gone forth.
Striking away the black skin... 491 Driving away the adversaries, O Soma, you flow as the exhilarating one who knows the sacred rites; drive away the people who follow the gods. 492
Flow forth with that stream by which you caused the sun to shine,
impelling the waters for mankind. Flow on, you who aided Indra to slay Vṛtra.
Flow around for this feast, O Indu, you who in your exhilarations struck down the nine-and-ninety fortresses that encompassed the great waters.
With your juice, flow for us toward the celestial, wealth-winning Bharadvāja. Resounding, flow into the filter.
The tawny bull has bellowed; he is great and beautiful to behold like Mitra.
He has shone together with the sun... We choose today your skillful, joy-bestowing bearer,
the protector who is desired by many.
O Adhvaryu, lead the Soma pressed with stones onto the filter;
purify it for Indra to drink. Crossing over, the exhilarating one flows—the stream of the pressed juice.
The gladdening one flows across;
flow hither, O Soma, bringing thousandfold wealth and heroic strength. Bestow upon us glorious renown.
The ancient Āyus have followed the newest path;
they brought forth the sun for the sake of light. Flow on, O Soma, most resplendent, roaring toward the wooden vats.
Sitting in the wombs, in the various births...
O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor; O God, you are a bull whose vows are manly. As a bull, you have established the sacred laws.
Flow for strength with your stream, being purified by the wise;
O Indu, go toward the cows with your luster. Flow, O Soma, as a bull seeking the gods, with a pleasant stream.
Seeking us with his pure streams,
he flows toward us; O Soma, through this skillful act, though already great, you have increased further, for as a bull you display your power.
This Pavamāna, the observer of all people, is established;
he takes notice as he is urged toward the great kinship. O Indu, bearing your wave like a ship, flow forth for our great [benefit].
The tireless one flows toward the gods; driving away the adversaries, Soma flows,
casting off the stingy ones as he goes to the appointed place of Indra.
Being purified with your stream, O Soma, you flow while clothing yourself in the waters. As a bestower of treasures, you sit upon the seat of Truth; you are a golden fountain, a god.
Pour out on every side the pressed juice—Soma, who is the supreme oblation.
He who, manly, having flowed within the waters, has pressed the Soma with the stones...
O Soma, pressed by the stones, through the sheep’s wool filter, like a man entering a city, the tawny one has settled into the two bowls; you have taken your place firmly among the wooden vessels.
O Soma, for the banquet of the gods, you have swelled like a river with its flood; with the milk of the stalk, exhilarating and wakeful, flow toward the honey-dripping vat.
O Soma, pressed by the pressers upon the backs of the sheep’s wool, you have flowed forth.
Like a bay mare, she goes with a golden stream; she goes with a pleasant stream. O Soma, O Indu, day after day I have taken delight in your friendship.
Many [obstacles], O tawny one, lie in wait for me; help me, pass beyond those enclosures.
Being cleansed by skillful hands, you send forth your voice into the ocean;
O Pavamāna, you flow toward us with abundant, tawny wealth that is much-desired.
The Soma-drops, the active ones, flow toward the exhilarating intoxication.
Upon the surface of the ocean, the wise ones, exhilarating and distilling intoxication, [flow].
O Soma, being purified, watchful and beloved, you pass through the woollen filters.
You have become a sage, the best of the Aṅgirases; sprinkle our sacrifice with honeyed sweetness.
The exhilarating Soma, pressed for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, flows pure;
with a thousand streams it rushes through the sheep’s wool, and the Āyus cleanse it.
Flow on, O best winner of booty, toward all desirable things!

You are the ocean; in the first ordinance, O exhilarating Soma, you flow for the gods. The purifying ones have been released in a stream across the filter. Accompanied by the Maruts, exhilarating, and impetuous like Indra’s steeds, they flow toward wisdom and sacrificial foods.
Run forth and settle in the vat; being purified by the men, flow toward the prize.
Cleansing you like a swift horse, they lead you with reins toward the sacred grass.
Proclaiming wisdom like Uśanas, the god declares the generations of the gods.
The one of great vows, the kinsman of purity, the purifier, approaches with his feet like a bellowing boar.

The bearer sends forth three voices: the thought of Truth and the inspired wisdom of the sacred word (*brahman*). Like cows seeking their lord, they go toward the master of the herd; like lowing thoughts, the prayers go toward Soma.

Being purified by this impulse and by the pressing-stones, the god has united his essence with the gods. Pressed out, he goes around the filter, singing like a Hotṛ-priest at the measured dwellings rich in cattle.
Soma flows clear, the progenitor of hymns, the progenitor of heaven, the progenitor of earth.
The progenitor of Agni, the progenitor of Sūrya, the progenitor of Indra, and the progenitor of Viṣṇu—
him, the three-backed, the bull, the bestower of vigor, the possessor of limbs, the singers have caused to low with their voices.
Dwelling in the woods like Varuṇa among the rivers, the bestower of jewels distributes desirable treasures.
The ocean has surged forth at the first ordinance, generating offspring as the guardian of the world.

The bull Soma, pressed upon the mountain-ridge of the woolly filter, has grown great; he is the roaring stone. The tawny one neighs loudly as he is released, settling within the belly of the wooden vessel while being purified.
When men prepare the garment for him, he comes from the cows; they generate the hymn through their own powers.
This very honeyed Soma of yours, O Indra, the bull, has flowed through the filter for you, the bull.
Bestowing thousands, bestowing hundreds, a giver of much, the prize-winner has taken his place upon the sacrificial grass for all time.

Flow on, O Soma, rich in sweetness, observer of the Eternal Law (Ṛta), clothing yourself in waters upon the sheep’s-wool back. Descend into the wooden vats filled with clarity; you are the most exhilarating, intoxicating drink for Indra.
The heroic leader of the armies goes at the head of the chariots, seeking cattle; his host rejoices.
Making the invocations of Indra auspicious for his friends, Soma puts on his impetuous garments.
Your honeyed streams have been let loose as you, purified, pass through the sheep’s wool filter. O Pavamāna, you flow to the domain of the cows, generating the sun and swelling with hymns.
Sing forth! Let us worship the gods; send forth Soma for great wealth.
Sweet, let him flow through the sheep’s wool filter; let the divine drop settle in the jar.
Being urged forward, the progenitor of heaven and earth has gone forth like a chariot to win the prize.
Going toward Indra, sharpening his weapons, and taking all treasures into his hands— when the speech of the longing mind fashioned him at the forefront of the heavenly Dharma of the Supreme One,
then the cows, lowing for their choice, came to him, the beloved lord, the Indu, in the jar.

The ten sisters, the flowing thoughts of the sage, together cleanse the one who sprinkles. The tawny one has run forth from his birthplace; like a prize-winning steed, he has reached the wooden vat. When the thoughts vie for him as beauties do for a stallion, they compete for the sun-like lord as subjects do for a king.
Choosing the waters, he flows as a sage, like a pen for the increase of cattle—this is my prayer.

The vigorous drop, Soma, flows into the milk-streams, bestowing strength upon Indra for his exhilaration. He slays the demon and drives away the enemy, creating wide space as the king of the assembly.
Flow onward with this [stream], flow with these riches; O Indu, flow forth into the vessel for me.

Even Bradhna, like the wind, bestowed his impetus upon him—the man of many wisdoms, the wise one, the lord. That great deed Soma the buffalo performed when, as the embryo of the waters, he chose the gods.

Pavamāna bestowed strength upon Indra; Indu generated light in the sun. (542) The eloquent one has been let loose like a chariot-horse in a race, the first inventor through inspired thought and wisdom. Ten sisters cleanse the bearer upon the sheep-wool ridge, toward the sacrificial seats. (543)
Like waves of water crossing over, our inspired thoughts surge forth toward Soma. Paying homage, they approach him; longing for him, they enter into him who longs for them.
Sixth Prapāṭhaka. Second Half.
1.6.2.0601a For you, from the fore-conquering juice, for the exhilarating pressed draught—
1.6.2.0601c Drive away the dog, O friends, the long-tongued one! 1.6.2.0602a This Pūṣan, this Bhaga, this wealth— Soma, being purified, flows onward.
The Lord of the entire universe has looked out upon both heaven and earth.
546 The pressed Soma juices, most rich in sweetness and exhilarating for Indra, have flowed through the filter. May your intoxications go to the gods. 547
The Soma drops flow for us, the best finders of the path;
they are friends, well-sounding, stainless, pious-minded, and winners of the light.
Pour forth for us wealth that is most effective in winning booty, a hundredfold desire.
O Indu, [we praise] you who bring a thousandfold bounty, who possess abundant splendor, and who overcome all adversaries.
(549) The guileless ones sing toward him, the beloved and desirable one of Indra. Like mothers licking their calf born at the first age, they caress him. (550)
For the one who is desirable and bold, they draw the bow as a manly deed;
bright rays spread forth for the Asura to clothe himself in, at the head of the inspired songs, seeking greatness.
They purify that desirable, golden-hued, brown one with the fleece of the wool.
He who goes forth with exhilaration beyond all the gods...
552 The mortal desires this speech as he presses out the juice of the plant; strike away the stingy hound, as the Bhr̥gus struck down Makha. 553
Well-disposed, he flows toward his dear names, upon which the mighty one grows strong.
The far-seeing, lofty one has mounted the wide-reaching chariot of the great Sūrya. Let our unurged drops flow forth, the golden ones, resounding loudly among the gods.
Even though the hostile powers consume our nourishments, may they remain as enemies to us; may our prayers win for us the prize.
This honeyed thunderbolt of Indra, the most beautiful of beauties, has roared within the vat.
Toward it flow the well-milking, butter-dropping cows, lowing with their milk.
The drop has gone to Indra’s appointed place; as a friend, he does not fail the agreement with his friend.
Like a youth with young women, Soma flows together into the jar by a hundredfold path.
The sustainer of heaven, the effective essence, the skill of the gods, he flows forth, to be celebrated by men.
Like a steed released by warriors, Hari spreads his splendors at will across the rivers.
The bull of hymns, the far-seeing Soma, flows on, the furtherer of days, of dawns, and of heaven.
The breath of the rivers, he has roared into the jars, entering the heart of Indra through the inspired poets.
For him, the seven cows have yielded thrice the true milk-mixture in the highest heaven.
He has fashioned four other beautiful worlds for his adornment, as he grew strong through the eternal laws (*ṛta*).
O Soma, flow forth well-pressed for Indra; let disease vanish along with the demons.
Let not the double-dealing ones delight in your juice; let the drops rich in wealth remain here.

Soma has been pressed, the ruddy bull, the tawny one; like a wondrous king, he has bellowed toward the cows. Purifying himself, he passes through the sheep’s wool filter; like a falcon, he has settled in his ghee-filled dwelling.
Toward the god, the honeyed drops have flowed forth like milch-cows;
seated upon the sacred grass (*barhis*), eloquent with their udders, they have taken for themselves the *parisrut* as a radiant garment.
They anoint it, they smear it, they anoint it thoroughly; they lick the ritual power (*kratu*) and balm it with sweetness.

Flow on with might in streams, O Indu, for the feast of the gods. O Soma, rich in sweetness, take your seat within our beaker.

May he not fail to provide sustenance; may he be pleased with our prayers. O Indu, when pressed, you are rich in cattle, rich in horses, and full of great skill like a wealthy man;
bestow upon us a pure color among the cows.
The voices have sung toward you, the finder of wealth, for our sake;

The beloved, golden-hued one flows through the winding channels with speed.
Flow forth to the praisers, bringing glory accompanied by heroic sons; purifying himself, Soma flows around the honey-dripping vat,
while the seven voices of the seers have sung their praise.
Flow on, O Soma, most rich in sweetness, the best provider of wisdom, the exhilarating draught for Indra; flow as the great, heaven-dwelling, most intoxicating draught.
O Lord of Food, O God, shine forth upon us with lofty splendor and glory for the one who seeks the gods.
Open the middle chest;
pour out the libation like a horse. Press the soma for him who is worthy of praise, the one who crosses the waters, who traverses the mid-air, who dwells in the woods, and who floats upon the flood.
This very one, the distiller of intoxication, the bull with a thousand streams who milks the sky,
bearing all treasures— he is pressed,
he who is the bringer of riches, the bringer of wealth, and the bringer of sacrificial offerings.
Soma, who [is the lord] of well-established dwellings...
You indeed, O Pavamāna, most radiant one, proclaim the divine generations for the sake of immortality.
This most intoxicating one, pressed out, flows with a stream through the sheep’s wool filter;
he sports like a wave of waters.
He who, by his might, has driven forth the cows that were within the mountain and among the ruddy kine.
You have stretched out toward the enclosure of cattle and horses; like one clad in armor, O bold one, break it open! Like one clad in armor, O bold one, break it open!
Thus ends the *pāvamāna* section, the *kāṇḍa* dedicated to Soma.

Indra is the king of the moving world and of men; he who, from above the earth, possesses every form.

Then he bestows riches upon the donor; may he impel prosperity even toward the one who praises him from nearby. For him, this realm is joined for the sake of the striving man, as a forest of light for Indra’s great and delightful domain.

With you, O Soma Pavamāna, may we continually win the prize in every battle.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us great wealth. Make me alone the bull;
he [is] for our Indra, who is worthy of sacrifice, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts.

O Vāyu, accompanied by the *niyuts*, come; this bright [soma] is offered to you.

O Maghavan, when you were born for the slaying of Vṛtra, you were unprecedented.
You spread out that earth and you propped up the sky.
May Parameṣṭhin Prajāpati establish splendor, fame, and the essence of the sacrifice within me, as firmly as the sky is fixed in heaven.
May your milks come together, and may your strengths, which overcome the malicious, unite;
swelling for the sake of immortality, O Soma, bestow upon yourself the highest glories in heaven.
You, O Soma, have generated all these plants, you have generated the waters, and you have generated the cows.

They conceived the first name of the cows—the thrice-seven supreme name of the people. Knowing this, the earth resounded; the ruddy cows appeared, manifesting with glory.
Some flow together, others come near; they fill the common reservoir, the rivers.

To him, the pure one, the shining one, the protector of the waters, the pure waters flow. The auspicious young woman has come forth; she strives to touch the banners of the day. The auspicious Night has become the resting place for the whole world.
Now for the great, ruddy bull Pṛkṣa, let our speech go forth to Jātavedas at the assembly.
A pure, new hymn flows clear like Soma for Vaiśvānara, as a lovely offering for Agni.
May all the gods hear my sacrifice, and may both Heaven and Earth and Apāṃ Napāt hear my prayer.
Let me not speak words that should be avoided; may we rejoice most intimately within your favor.
May glory be mine from Heaven and Earth, may glory be mine from Indra and Bṛhaspati;
may I obtain the glory of Bhaga, and may glory be bestowed upon me.
May I be glorious; may I be the one who proclaims her assembly. I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, those which the wielder of the thunderbolt performed for the first time.
He slew the serpent Ahi, he pierced the water-channels, and he split open the bellies of the mountains.
I am Agni, Jātavedas by birth; clarified butter is my eye, and nectar is in my mouth.
I am the threefold light, the measurer of the mid-world (*rajas*), the imperishable radiance, and the oblation—everything.
Agni protects the foremost step of the bird, the inspired singer; the mighty one protects the course of the sun.
Agni protects the seven-headed one in his center...
When kindled, O Agni, your radiant tongue moves within the mouth, shining brightly. As such, O Agni, finder of wealth, grant us milk, prosperity, and splendor so that we may behold it.
Delighting now in spring, delighting now in summer;
delighting through the rains, the autumns, the winter, and the cool season.
The Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet.
Having encompassed the earth on all sides, he stood ten fingers' breadth beyond it.
The Puruṣa rose up three-quarters of his height; one quarter of him remained here again.
Thus he pervaded everything, both that which eats and that which does not eat.

The Person alone is all this—whatever has been and whatever is to be. All beings constitute one quarter of him; his three quarters are the immortal in heaven. Such is his greatness, and the Person is even greater than that.
And he is the lord of immortality, who by means of food grows beyond [all]. From him Virāj was born; from Virāj was born Puruṣa.
Once born, he extended beyond the earth behind and also before.
I honor you two, Heaven and Earth, most bountiful, who have spread yourselves out over immeasurable distance.
O Heaven and Earth, be gracious; deliver us from distress.
O Indra, your two bay steeds are like your beard, and they are indeed golden-yellow.
The sages and men who dwell in the forest praise you;
with that splendor which belongs to gold, or the splendor which belongs to cattle,
and the splendor of true Brahman— thereby we unite you.

O Indra, bestow upon us that strength which is yours; for you, O Virapśin, are the master of this great [power]. Like our will, make our manly vigor, our steadfast strength, and our booty such that we may slay the enemies among the Vṛtras.
Let them rise up together with their bulls and their calves, bearing all forms, the twice-drinking cows.
May this wide and spacious world be yours; may these waters be easy to drink here.
O Agni, you purify our lives; speed forth strength and nourishment for us. Drive far away misfortune.
May the wide-striding one drink the Soma-mead; may he bestow unimpaired life upon the lord of the sacrifice.
Impelled by the wind, he who protects by his own power nourishes all creatures and shines forth in many ways.
The wondrous host of the gods has risen—the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.

The Sun has filled heaven, earth, and the intermediate space; he is the soul of all that moves and stands still. This spotted bull has come and has settled before his mother; and as he goes toward the light, he approaches his father.
Moving within, his light flows from the out-breath to the in-breath;
the Great One has illumined the sky. He shines across thirty realms; speech is bestowed upon the bird.
Day after day,
through the nights, those stars depart like thieves,
before the Sun who beholds all things.
His banners have been seen; his rays extend across the peoples like blazing fires.
O Sūrya, you are the one who crosses over, visible to all, the maker of light.
You illuminate the entire radiant realm.
Facing the clans of the gods, facing humanity, you rise up; facing all, you are for the beholding of the heavenly light.

O Purifier, with that eye wherewith you behold the people as they stir about, O Varuṇa, you look upon them. You rise up toward the height, measuring out the broad space with your rays through the nights.
Beholding his births as the sun,
Sūrya has yoked the seven bright ones, the granddaughters of the chariot;
with them, self-yoked, he goes.
"Seven bay horses carry you on your chariot, O divine Sūrya, you whose hair is flame, O far-seeing one. Thus ends the Āraṇyaka section, the Kāṇḍa.
O Maghavan, find [us]! Find a path; you have praised the quarters of the sky. O Lord of powers, O possessor of many riches, grant us aid for our many [deeds]. 641

you who are the most generous among the patrons— like a stalk of soma, a flame of light, O wise one, lead us; Indra knows that, praise him!

We invoke Indra for the winning of wealth, the unconquered conqueror.
May he, the winner of light, drive away our enemies; may he, the winner of light, drive away our enemies.
O wielder of the stone, that stalk of yours which was for exhilaration—bestow favor upon us, O Vasu; O most powerful one, your abundance is praised.
For Śakra is surely the master; let us now lay down this new [hymn].
O Lord, slayer of Vṛtra, let us two speak together in the assemblies of men—of that hero who goes forth for the sake of cattle, our friend, most gracious and free from guile.

Toward that Soma, which is difficult to master, men [direct] their all-encompassing prayer.

As a son, he establishes for his parents a secret third name upon the luminous realm of heaven. Shining brightly, he has bellowed toward the jars; guided by the men, he is held within the golden vessel.
4.1.1.19 They have sung forth the milking of the *ṛta*; you, O three-backed one, shine abroad over the dawns.
4.1.1.20 At every sacrifice, with song after song, we shall praise Agni for his skill;
we shall proclaim the immortal Jātavedas, like a beloved friend.
O Son of Strength, may he indeed be well-disposed toward us; let us serve him for the giving of oblations.
May he be our protector in battles, may he be our increaser, and may he be the savior of our bodies.
Come here, O Agni, so that I may speak these other songs to you.
May you grow strong by these drops,
O Indu, wherever you set your mind upon a higher skill;
there you shall prepare your seat.

For you, O Lord of the Earth, have never failed to bestow the merit of our offerings; therefore, we seek to win your favor. O Unprecedented One, we, seeking your protection, carry you as if you were a sturdy pillar.
We invoke the wondrous wielder of the thunderbolt... For the sake of aid in this rite, we have approached you; that fierce one of yours who is bold has come to us.
O Indra, we friends have chosen you as our protector, the winner of spoils.
Therefore, O Indra, lover of songs, we approach you with desire; we have poured forth our prayers like waters flowing upward.
O Hero, the sacred hymns increase your vital strength with their youthful invocations.
O wielder of the stone, though you have grown great day by day, they yoke the two bay steeds of the impetuous one with song— upon the broad chariot with its wide yoke, harnessed by a word,
the bearers of Indra who find the light of heaven.

4.1.2.01.01a Sing forth unto Indra for the drinking of your soma-juice;
4.1.2.01.01c him who conquers all, the lord of a hundred powers, the most bountiful among the people. 713
Call him Puruhūta, Puruṣṭuta, Gāthānya, and Sanasruta;
say, "He is Indra.
Indra is the giver of great spoils to us, the dancer of strength.
4 1 2 01 03c Great is he who has attained higher knowledge...
715 4 1 2 02 01a Sing forth a gladdening song for Indra, the lord of bay horses; 4 1 2 02 01c O friends, [sing] for the drinker of Soma... 716
O bounteous one, let him recite the hymn of praise, as men have done for you who dwell in heaven, so that we may perform [service] for you whose wealth is true.

In whom all glories rejoice and the seven assemblies meet— that Indra we invoke when the Soma is pressed. At the Trikadruka rites, the gods performed the sacrifice that brings consciousness.
May our songs of praise increase him.
This Soma of yours, O Indra, has been purified upon the sacred grass; come here, hasten to it, and drink.

O Ākhaṇḍala, you are invoked.
That which is your Kuṇḍapāyya [offering], O grandson of the bull-like horned one, [is for] the great-grandson.

Washed by men with stones, purified all around by the strainers, he is like a horse bathed in rivers. We have made him sweet for you, mixing him with milk like barley.
O Indra, I am here with you at this shared feast... (736) For this [Soma] has been pressed by strength, O Lord of bounties;
drink of it, O lover of songs! (737)
O you who sit according to your own nature, when the soma is pressed, restrain your body; may he, the Soma-drinker, exhilarate you.
May it reach your two flanks, O Indra, and may it reach your head through this sacred prayer (*brahman*).
O Hero, stretch forth your arms with bounty!
Come hither; let these [singers] sit down near Indra; sing forth to him, O friends who bring hymns of praise.
To him who is most abundant among the many,

With strengths, come to our invocation...

Rising together with the sun, the radiant star, the sun releases the ruddy cows. O Dawn, at your dawning and that of the sun, may we attain a share of the food.
These morning sacrifices, O Aśvins, call upon you both at dawn. I here invoke you for protection, O lords of power, for you go to every clan.
You two, O heroes, bestow wondrous nourishment; impel it toward the one who offers true praise.

Like the sun, he is visible to all; he rushes toward the lakes and the seven downward-flowing rivers unto heaven. Purifying himself, he stands above all the worlds.
Soma is a god like the sun. This god, pressed for the gods according to his ancient birth,
the tawny one, flows through the filter.
This god, through his ancient hymn, has grown great among the gods;
the seer has been magnified by the inspired singer.
Yielding that ancient milk, you are poured out around the filter.

Pressed for Indra, Vāyu, Varuṇa, and the Maruts.

The beloved, bright one has clothed himself in his garment; like a dear son, he is to be groomed. The skillful workers urge him forth with their hands as they would a chariot in the rivers.
Let the Soma drops, distilling exhilaration, flow for the glory of our patrons.
The pressed juices have stepped forth into the assembly;
like a swan to its flock, they have caused the thought of every man to resound. Like a steed, he is adorned with milk.
At first, the maidens of Trita urge the tawny one with the stones—the drop for Indra’s drinking.
Flow on with this [song], O god-seeking one; chanting, you go around the filter from every side.

Flow toward the worshippers with glory accompanied by heroic sons.

Flow on as the leader of speech, O Soma, with your wondrous aids,
toward all poetic insights. You, the leader, stirring the waters of the ocean, impel our voices.
Flow on, O you who belong to all people! For you, O Sage, these worlds have been established for the sake of your greatness, O Soma;

Flow on, O Indu, as the pressed bull; make us glorious among the people.
Strike away all our enemies. In whose friendship we may overcome those who attack us.
O Indu, your splendor is supreme... Your terrible weapons, which are sharp for striking down, exist;
protect us from every reviler.
O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor; O God, you are a bull whose ordinances are bull-like. As a bull, you have established the sacred laws.
Bull is your manly power, bull is the wood, and bull is the pressed juice.
O Bull, you are indeed a bull;
like a horse, the bull has neighed. O Indu, bring together the cows and the steeds. Open for us the doors to wealth.
For you are indeed a bull by your radiance; we invoke you, the brilliant one, O Pavamāna, the beholder of heaven. When you are sprinkled with waters and cleansed by the Āyus, you flow.
4.2.1.04.02c You attain your dwelling place in the *droṇa* vessel.
