We choose for ourselves the friendship of you, Pavamāna, as you rise up toward the filter.
Those waves of yours which flow across the filter in a stream—
With those [powers], O Soma, have mercy on us. Being purified, bring to us wealth and food accompanied by heroes;
for you, O Soma, are the master from every side.
We choose Agni as our messenger, the invoker, the all-knowing,
the skillful performer of this sacrifice. They ever invoke Agni with invocations, the lord of the people, again and again.
O Agni, bearer of oblations, beloved by many, bring the gods here for the one who has strewn the sacrificial grass; being born,
you are our adorable Hotṛ-priest.
We invoke Mitra and Varuṇa for the drinking of Soma— those two who are born with purified willpower,
who increase the cosmic order through the cosmic order, and who are the lords of the light of the cosmic order.
I invoke those two, Mitra and Varuṇa.
May Varuṇa be our protector and Mitra with all his aids;
may they both make us richly blessed.
To Indra indeed the singers sing loudly; to Indra, the reciters with their hymns;
Indra the voices have shouted after.
Indra alone is joined with the two bay steeds, mingled with the one yoked by word.
Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the golden one... O Indra, protect us in battles for booty and in contests for a thousandfold prizes, you, the fierce one,
with your fierce aids.
Indra raised the sun high in heaven for far-reaching vision;
he split the mountain asunder with his rays. To Indra and Agni we offer great homage and well-fashioned hymns.
With prayer and songs, seeking aid... for they, the wise ones, ever thus invoke them for protection;
impelled, they call for the winning of booty.
We, praising you with songs and offering oblations, call upon you both,
desiring to win the prize at the sacrifice.
Flow on as a bull with your stream, O exhilarating one, for the sake of the Maruts.
Bestowing [light] upon the quarters with his might...
him, O Pavamāna, you who see the sun, the sustainer of the two worlds,
the prize-winner, I urge on for the sake of spoils.
Flow with your stream, O tawny one, being perceived by the purifying [filter],
and urge on our ally in the contests for booty.
The red bull, bellowing toward us, goes along making the earth and the heaven resound.
Like the roar of Indra, your sound is heard in the battle; urging it forth, you flow with this voice.
806 Worthy of being tasted, swelling with milk, you go forth impelling the honeyed stalk.
O Pavamāna, as you are being poured out for Indra, O Soma, you go creating a continuous stream. 807
Flow thus, O exhilarating one, for intoxication, bending down the weapon of the one who seizes the heights;
bearing your radiant color all around, flow for us, O Soma, seeking cattle when poured out.
For we, the poets, invoke you alone for the winning of booty.

O Indra, Lord of the virtuous, men call upon you in battles against the Vṛtras; they call upon you in the races for the prize. O wondrous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, when you are praised with boldness, O Lord of the pressing-stones, bestow upon us cattle and chariot-horses, O Indra, like the total spoil won by a victor.
Sing forth to Indra, the giver of good gifts, for you as he is known—he, the bounteous lord of many riches, who bestows upon his singers as if with a thousandfold hand.
Like one with a hundred hosts, he advances boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the sake of the donor.
Like streams from a mountain, the gifts of him who nourishes many have overflowed.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, eager men made you swell yesterday;
O Indra, you who are borne by hymns, hear us here and come to our dwelling.
O fair-cheeked one, O possessor of bay horses, rejoice; we implore you. Through you, the wise ones adorn themselves.
Your glories are supreme and worthy of hymns, O Indra, lover of songs, when the juices are pressed. Flow on with that exhilarating draught of yours which is most excellent.
O God-finder,
slayer of the wicked, you have struck down the hostile Vṛtra; day by day you are the winner of booty, the winner of cattle, and the winner of horses.
Mixed with the ruddy [Soma], you have become like cows easy to tend;
sit down like a falcon upon your nest. This Pūṣan, this wealth, this Bhaga—Soma, being purified, flows onward.
The Lord of the entire universe has looked out upon both heaven and earth.
The dear cows have lowed together for exhilaration, they who are eager;
the Soma drops, as they flow clear, prepare the paths.
O Pavamāna, bring that which is most powerful and worthy of renown, that wealth which surpasses the five tribes, by which we may win the forests.
The far-seeing Soma, the bull of prayers, flows clear; he is the prolonger of days, of dawns, and of heaven.

The life-breath of the rivers has bellowed toward the jars, entering the heart of Indra through the inspired poets. By the inspired poets, the ancient seer flows clear, guided by men as he hastens around the vessels;
generating the name of Trita, pouring forth sweetness, and strengthening Vāyu for friendship with Indra.
This one, being purified, has caused the dawns to shine; this one has become the maker of space for the rivers.
This Soma, milking the thrice-seven [cows] for the milk-mixture, flows as a delightful and exhilarating draught for the heart.
For such indeed you are, O hero-seeker; such indeed you are, O brave and steadfast one.
Thus may your mind be won over;
thus has the gift been established by all the ordainers, O you of most abundant wealth.
And so, O Indra, be with us.
O Lord of strength, be swift like a priest; O Master of spoils, be present here. Rejoice in the pressed juice mixed with milk.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as vast as the ocean.
The best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils—
O Indra, Lord of Might, in your friendship may we, possessing strength, never fear. We cry out toward you, the unconquered conqueror.

These swift drops have been poured through the filter toward all auspicious blessings;
driving away many misfortunes, the prize-winners provide easy paths for our offspring.
Making for themselves swift steeds,
they flow toward the hymn of praise, creating wide space for the cattle;
may they grant us continuous nourishment.
The King, Pavamāna, is impelled by prayers toward the mind,
in order to travel through the intermediate space.
O Soma, bring us conquering speed and beauty for the sake of splendor.
Pressed for the feast of the gods...
834 O Indu, bring to us a hundredfold increase of cattle and noble horses; bring the gift of fortune for our protection.
We approach you, who bring manly powers to the gathering places of the great heaven,
the lovely one, with our skillful work. We seek the exhilarating drink, which overcomes the bold, is worthy of praise, and possesses most mighty ordinances.
A hundred fortresses did he shatter, O you of many wondrous deeds; from there, wealth came toward you, the king, O wise one,
as the unwavering, well-winged bird brought it from heaven.
Then, being urged forth, he attained his supreme Indra-power and greatness— he who brings aid to those who seek it, the one who observes all people.

The singer bears up the guardian of the eternal Law. Flow for our nourishment with your stream, being purified by the wise;
O Indu, go toward the cows with your luster.

Purifying yourself, O lover of songs, create wide space and strength for the people; O tawny one, being released, flow toward the milk-mixture. Purifying yourself, go to the appointed place of Indra for the feast of the gods.

O Indra, even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths belonging to you,

These purified, wise Soma juices, mixed with curd, are like brilliant heroes— beautiful to behold, moving swiftly, and established in the clarified butter.
Pressed out by the stones, they have been gathered upon the ox-hide.
4.4.1.20 May those who find wealth sound forth nourishment for us from every side.
4.4.1.21 Flow with this purification, O Indu; flow toward these riches. Pour yourself forth into the lake, O drop.
Even Braghna, like the wind, bestowed his speed upon him—upon the man of many wisdoms, O Sage, you have granted [it] to the wise one.
And flow for us with this purifying power at the famous ford of Śravāyya.
Like Naiguta, shake down sixty thousand treasures for the battle, like ripe fruit from a tree. Great indeed are these two names of his, O Bull: Māṃścatva and Pṛśana, for the striking of the foe.

4.4.1.21. You have lulled the secret ones to sleep and softened the enemies; you have struck down the senseless one. 4.4.1.22. O Agni, be our closest kinsman, our protector, and our auspicious shelter.
4.4.1.22. As the Vasu, Agni, renowned for wealth, come hither; most brilliant, grant us riches.
We now entreat you, O most radiant and shining one, for the sake of our well-being and for our friends.
May we, together with Indra and all the gods, bring these worlds into harmony.
May Indra, along with the Ādityas, establish for us the sacrifice, our bodies, and our progeny.
4.4.1.23 Indra, together with the Ādityas and the host of Maruts, shall provide medicines for us.
4.4.1.24 Sing forth a song to Indra, the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, the inspired sage, whom he delights.
4.4.1.24 The Maruts, skilled singers, sing their hymn; that renowned and youthful Indra utters his roar.
Dwelling near the honey-sweet spring, may we prosper; we meditate upon that wealth of yours, O Indra.
The Fourth Chapter. Second Half.
Proclaiming poetic wisdom like Uśanas, the god declares the generations of the gods.
The one of great vows, whose kin are pure, the purifier, approaches the place like a boar, singing aloud.
The swans, the impetuous ones, have come toward the sound; the bull-like herds have gone down to their home.
Together, O friends, they proclaim the invincible song, the lowing of the purifying Pavamāna who seeks the dwelling.
He has harnessed the speed of the wide-striding one; like cattle, they measure him as he sports at will.
The sharp-horned one makes himself vast; by day he appears golden, by night he is dappled brown.
Resounding like chariots, they have come forth like horses seeking aid.
The Soma juices have flowed forth for the sake of wealth,
like chariots urged forward; they have run between the hands like the prizes of singers.
The kings [are adorned] not with praises; the Soma drops are adorned with milk, like the sacrifice by the seven creators. The pressed drops, for exhilaration, flow around with great power and song.
The sweet [streams] flow in a stream;
the Soma juices, reaching Vivasvat, quicken the fortune of the dawns. The suns spread across the fine [filter].
Through the gateway of inspired thoughts, the ancient singers open the way;
the Āyus [attain] the impetuous force of the Bull. The seven-born Hotṛ-priests have come together in unison.

The Sun beholds with his eye the beloved station of heaven, which was placed in secret by the *adhvaryu* priests.
The glorious drops have been poured forth upon the path according to the law of Truth.
Knowing his courses,
the foremost stream of honey plunges into the great waters; he,
worthy of praise among all oblations, [is the sacrifice].
The bull, the foremost of speech, has bellowed forth toward the wood;
the true sacrifice proceeds toward the dwellings. When the sage, purifying his manly powers, flows around with his poetic wisdom.
The prize-winning steed desires to win;
Pavamāna sits over his rivals like a king among the clans when the wise ones release him.
On the day of the wind, the beloved tawny one settles within the woods; as a singer, he is implored with a hymn. Together with exhilaration, he goes to Vāyu, Indra, and the Aśvins.
Those who, by his law, [are] in battle...
1134 The waves of honey flow toward Mitra, Varuṇa, and Bhaga, made known through his powers. 1135
O Heaven and Earth, grant us wealth for the winning of honeyed strength,
glory, and the gathering of riches.
Today we choose from you the skillful, bliss-bringing bearer of the sacrifice.
To the one who protects, who is desired by many...
1137 To the delightful one, to the excellent one, to the inspired one, to the wise one; To the one who protects, who is desired by many... 1138
Bring hither wealth with kindly intent, O you of noble power, unto our bodies; bring the protector who is desired by many.
Agni Vaiśvānara, the head of heaven, the messenger of earth, born in the Eternal Order (Ṛta).

The great sovereigns,
Mitra and Varuṇa, both whose source is clarified butter, are encompassed by great majesty;

May you two be able to grant us great earthly and celestial wealth. Great is your dominion among the gods.
O Indra of wondrous luster, come; these pressed juices long for you.

O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, come swiftly to our sacred hymns;

The black one makes [him] with her tongue...

Like a young man with maidens, Soma rushes together into the jar by a hundred-pathed way. Your thoughts, joyous, praiseworthy, and worthy of honor, have stepped forth into the enclosures. They have shouted toward the golden-hued one as he plays; the milch-cows have been milked with their own milk.
O Soma, O Indu, as you are being purified, flow for us with your wave, bringing abundant and swelling nourishment—
food that yields for us thrice daily, inexhaustible, rich in cattle, full of strength, sweet, and endowed with heroic power.
No one by any deed can reach him who has performed this work that ever prospers.
Like Indra, who is praised by all through sacrifices, the skillful, the unassailable, the bold in his might— him, the unconquerable,
the fierce, the victor in battles, at whose birth the great,
wide-extended milch-cows lowed together; heaven and earth lowed with joy.
O friends, sit down and sing forth to him who is being purified;

Purify the exhilarating draught that brings double strength for the gods,
which accomplishes skillful power, so that it may be most soothing for the host [of Maruts] to enjoy, and for Mitra and Varuṇa.

The prize-winning one has flowed forth, with a thousand streams, across the filter, through the sheep’s wool. That prize-winner, possessing a thousandfold seed, being cleansed by the waters and mixed with milk, has flowed forth.
O Soma, go forth into the belly of Indra, guided by the men and pressed by the stones.
Those Soma juices which have been pressed in the distance, those which have been pressed nearby, or those which [are pressed] at Śaryaṇāvat;
those among the Ārjīkas, among the Kr̥tvas, or those in the midst of the dwellings.
Or those who [dwell] among the five peoples— may they pour down rain for us from heaven, and [bestow] great heroic strength; the Soma drops,
the resounding gods.
May Vatsa draw your mind hither, even from the highest dwelling place;
O Agni, I desire you with my song.
For you are present in many places, the Lord over all the quarters.
In battles we invoke you... Seeking strength, we invoke Agni for protection in battles,
him who bestows wondrous wealth in the contests for booty.
O Indra, bring us strength and manly vigor, O Lord of a hundred powers, O far-seeing one;
bring a hero who conquers in battle. For you, O gracious Lord of a hundred powers, have become our father and our mother.
Now we pray for thy favor... O impetuous one, much-invoked, strengthened by power, I address thee who art eager for the prize; grant us heroic strength.
O Indra, O Wondrous One, O Wielder of the Stone, if that gift bestowed by you is not here with me, O Finder of Wealth, bring it to us with both your hands. O Indra,
bring that which you deem most excellent and celestial.
May we know you, O boundless giver of gifts. With that far-reaching mind of yours which is renowned and vast throughout the quarters, O wielder of the stone,
break open even the firmest things to win us booty.
Fifth Chapter. First Half.

They cleanse and adorn the beloved infant as soon as he is born; the Maruts with their host adorn the inspired singer. Being a seer through his poetic songs and a sage through his wisdom, Soma goes singing across the filter.
The one whose mind is that of a seer, who makes himself a seer, the winner of light through his own power, the leader of a thousand songs,
the pathfinder for the sages— the mighty Soma, desiring to win the third realm, shines as sovereign following the Virāj.
The hawk seated in the vessels, the far-reaching bird, the drop that finds the cattle, bearing his weapons.
4.5.1.01 Following the wave of the waters, the buffalo proclaims the ocean, the fourth station.
4.5.1.02 These Soma juices have flowed toward the beloved desire of Indra,
increasing his heroic power.
Purifying themselves, seated in the vessels, and going toward Vāyu and the Aśvins— may they bestow upon us great heroic strength.
O Soma, being purified for the sake of Indra’s bounty, impel his heart.
To sit upon the womb of the gods...
(1180) The ten fingers cleanse you; the seven prayers impel you. The sages have rejoiced after you. (1181)

For the exhilaration of the gods, we release you through the sheep’s fleece; as you flow, we clothe you with the milk of cows. Purifying yourself in the jars, the ruddy, golden-hued one puts on his garments.
He has clothed himself in the products of the cow. Flow for us toward the liberal patrons; strike away all our enemies.
O Indu, enter into your friend.
May we partake of you, who beholds men, who are drunk by Indra, and who finds the light of heaven—may we obtain offspring and nourishment.
Flow forth from the sky as rain; flow from the earth as splendor.
O Soma, bestow strength upon us in battles.
Soma, being purified, flows in a thousand streams through the sheep’s wool,
to the appointed place of Vāyu and Indra.
O you who seek protection, sing forth to Pavamāna, the inspired sage,
who has been pressed for the banquet of the gods.
The Soma drops, possessing thousandfold power, flow forth for the winning of the prize.
Being praised for the banquet of the gods...
And flow for us, for the winning of booty, with great refreshments; O Indu, [bestow] resplendent, heroic strength.
Like steeds urged on by their drivers, they have been let loose for the winning of booty;
the swift ones have passed through the sheep’s wool filter. May they flow for us with wealth in thousands and with heroic strength.
The pressed-out divine drops flow forth like lowing mothers toward their calf;
they have run from the hands [of the priests].
O Pavamāna, roaring loudly, flow as an exhilarating draught beloved by Indra;
strike away all our enemies.
O Pavamānas, who behold the light of heaven, drive off the stingy ones.
Sit in the womb of the Truth. The Soma drops,
the pressed juices, have been released in a stream of Truth for Indra— most full of sweetness.
The inspired singers have sung aloud to Indra for the drinking of the soma, as milch-cows low to their calf.
The wise one, distilling exhilaration, dwells upon the wave of the river in his seat.
Soma rests upon Gaurī;
far-seeing at the navel of heaven, he is magnified in the fleece of the sheep. Soma is the wise seer of excellent insight.
The Soma which has been placed within the jars, set upon the filter— Indu has embraced it from all sides. Indu sends forth his voice from the summit of the ocean.
Stirring the honey-dripping vessel,
the tree whose hymn is constant, yielding milk within,
impels the human companions.

O Pavamāna, bestow upon us wealth of thousandfold luster; O Indu, grant us that which is self-sustaining. The sage, the inspired poet of heaven, being pressed, flows toward the beloved [waters] in a stream.
Soma is impelled in the distance...
Your vital energies rise up like the roar of a river’s wave;
sharpen the point of the arrow!
At your birth, three voices eager for the sacrifice rise up,
when you go upon the back of the sheep’s wool. With the stones they urge the beloved tawny one through the fleece of the sheep.
4.5.1.05.03c Pavamāna, who drips with honey...
1207 4.5.1.05.04a Flow hither, O most exhilarating one, through the filter in a stream, O Sage, 4.5.1.05.04c To sit upon the seat of the hymn. 1208
Flow on, O most exhilarating one, anointed with milk and with rays; enter the belly of Indra. Flow around with this food, O Indu, you who are present in the intoxications.
He struck down nine-and-ninety fortresses at once for Divodāsa, who was thus intent upon his purpose— he struck down Śambara,
as well as that Turvaśa and Yadu.
O Indu, finder of horses, flow for us with horses, with cattle, and with gold;
pour forth thousandfold nourishments. Striking down our adversaries, Soma flows away from the stingy ones.
Going to the appointed place of Indra, bring us great wealth; O Pavamāna, slay our enemies. Bestow upon us, O Indu, glory accompanied by heroic sons.

Neither a hundred nor a thousand [enemies] have hindered you when you desire to bestow wealth, as you purify yourself and act like a sacrificial steed. Flow on with this stream by which you caused the sun to shine.
Being urged on toward the human waters...
Sūrya has yoked Etaśa; Pavamāna has yoked him at the mind for traveling through the intermediate space.
And those bay steeds of the Sun he has yoked to his chariot to travel,
while the Indu, crying out "Indra!",
[proceeds]. O [worshippers], with your fires, make Agni— the god who is most skilled in sacrifice— the messenger at the rite, being in harmony with the fires.
He who is steadfast among mortals, the upholder of *ṛta*, whose head is flame, whose food is ghee, the purifier—
like a neighing horse eager for pasture, when he has stepped forth from the great enclosure,
then the wind blows after his blaze; and indeed, thy path is black.
When you have been raised up, O Agni, the bull newly born, your ageless kindling-sticks move as they are enkindled.
Your ruddy smoke rises toward heaven; for you, O Agni, go as a messenger to the gods.
We incite that Indra for the sake of great power, to slay Vṛtra.
He has become a bull, a stallion;
Indra is made for giving, he is established as the most powerful in strength. Resplendent, worthy of praise, he is the one to whom Soma belongs.
Like a thunderbolt forged by speech, he is powerful and unshakable; fierce and invincible, he has grown strong.
O Adhvaryu, lead the pressed Soma through the filter with the stones.
4 5 1 11 01c Purify [the soma] for Indra to drink... 1225 4 5 1 11 02a Of that sweet juice of yours, O Indu, the gods have partaken;

Press out for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the most excellent nectar of heaven,
the Soma, most rich in sweetness.
The sustainer of heaven, the effective essence, the skillful power of the gods, flows clear, he who is to be celebrated by men.
Like a steed let loose by warriors, Hari spreads his splendors at will across the rivers;
like a hero, he takes weapons in his hands, a charioteer seeking to win cattle in the raids.
Stirring up the might of Indra with skillful works, the drop, urged forward, is anointed by the wise.
O Soma Pavamāna, entering Indra’s bellies with your wave, increasing in strength;
swell for us like lightning in the cloud, filling both worlds; through our prayer, bestow upon us eternal strengths.
O Indra, when you are invoked by men from the east, the west, the north, or the south—

O Sima, you are impelled by many men; you are for Anu, O bold one, and for Turvaśa. Or when, O Indra, you rejoice together with Ruma, Ruśama, Śyāvaka, and Kṛpa—may the Kaṇvas, who bring prayers, draw you hither with their hymns, O Indra; come!
May Indra hear both [calls] of ours; may he turn hither to this speech.
May the most powerful Maghavan come with his focused thought for the drinking of the Soma.
For him, the two worlds have fashioned as their self-ruling bull by means of their power.
4.5.1.14 You sit down as the first of those who possess similes, for your mind desires Soma.
4.5.1.15 Flow on, O God, for the sake of long life; let your exhilaration go to Indra. Ascend to Vāyu according to the cosmic law (dharman).
O Pavamāna Soma, you bestow upon us wealth worthy of renown; O Indu, enter the ocean. Striking down our adversaries, O Soma, you flow as the exhilarating finder of wisdom.
Drive away the people who seek the gods [for their own ends].
Flow toward us, O Indu, that wealth which best wins the prize, which is desired by hundreds, which brings thousands, and which possesses great splendor and overwhelming power.
O Vasu, may we be the ones most closely attuned to this wealth of yours, which is desired by many; O Ādhriyu, may we abide in your favor.
This Indu, the roaring one, flows through the sheep’s wool, distilling exhilarating joy.
4 5 1 16 03c Like a stream rising upward at the sacrifice, he goes forth with brilliance, seeking cattle.

1240 4 5 1 16 04a Flow clear, O Soma, as a great ocean, the father of the gods, through all abodes. 1241 4 5 1 16 05a Flow pure for the gods, O Soma, for heaven, for earth, and for the welfare of all creatures. 1242
4 5 1 16 06a You are the sustainer of heaven, the bright nectar; flow on, O steed, according to the true ordinance.
1243 4 5 1 18 01a I praise your most beloved guest, like a dear friend, O Agni, who is to be known like a chariot. 1244
Like a seer worthy of praise, whom the gods have established among mortals from of old— O youngest one, protect the men who offer oblations and hear our songs.
Protect our offspring and ourselves as well. O Indra, come to us, you who are dear, the ever-conquering,
the unconcealable, broad on all sides like a mountain, the Lord of Heaven.
For you, O true drinker of Soma, have indeed encompassed both worlds, O Indra; you are the strengthener of the presser and the lord of heaven.
For you, O Indra, are the upholder of all the eternal fortresses.
The slayer of the Dasyus, the prosperer of Manu, the lord of heaven...
(1249) The breaker of forts, the youth, the sage of immeasurable power was born;
Indra, the sustainer of every deed, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the much-praised one. (1250)
O wielder of the stone, you opened the cave of Vala, who possessed the cattle;
the gods, being urged on, came to you without fear. They have celebrated with hymns Indra, the lord by his might.
He whose gifts are a thousand, or even more—
Fifth Prapāṭhaka, Second Half:
The ocean roared at the first establishment of order, generating offspring, the guardian of the world.
4.5.2.01 The bull Soma, pressed upon the sheep’s-wool filter, has grown great on its ridge; he is the sounding stone.
4.5.2.02 Make Vāyu rejoice for our desire and for bounty; make Mitra and Varuṇa rejoice as you are being purified.
Make the host of Maruts rejoice, make the gods rejoice, and make Heaven and Earth rejoice, O divine Soma.
That great Soma, the mighty one, performed this deed when, as the embryo of the waters, he chose the gods.
As Pavamāna, he bestowed vigor upon Indra; as Indu, he generated light in the sun.
This immortal god flies like a winged bird.
He descends into the wooden vats to settle therein;
this god, praised by the sages, plunges into the waters,
bestowing jewels upon the donor.
Like a hero going forth with his warriors, this Pavamāna seeks to win all desirable things.
This god, as he flows clear, speeds along like a chariot; he bestows wealth upon us.
He reveals his resonant voice...
This god, Pavamāna, is cleansed by those who praise him, who love the Truth— the tawny one, for the sake of booty.
This god, made ready by wisdom, runs across the obstacles;
he is Pavamāna, the invincible.
He runs through heaven with his stream, across the regions of space.
4.5.2.02.07c Pavamāna, bellowing loudly...
1262 4.5.2.02.08a This one has pervaded the sky, having passed through the regions unimpeded;
4.5.2.02.08c Pavamāna, the one of excellent sacrifice... 1263
By his ancient birth, this god, pressed for the gods, the tawny one, flows through the filter. He, the one of many vows, being born, engendering nourishments—
4 5 2 02 10c Pressed, he flows in a stream...
1265 4 5 2 03 01a This hero goes by means of subtle wisdom, with swift chariots, 4 5 2 03 01c going to the appointed place of Indra. 1266
He is meditated upon by many with profound thought for the sake of the great host of gods,
where the immortals have attained their goal. Men cleanse him who is worthy of cleansing within the wooden vats.
Bestowing great nourishment upon the earth... when the impetuous ones urge him on... this [Soma], once set in motion, is led forth along the path that purifies within.
When the swift ones strike him... 1268–1269.
He goes forth with golden ornaments, with brilliant rays, like a prize-winning steed; becoming the lord of the rivers. He, the bull of the herd, brandishing his horns, whets them sharp.

The ten fingers urge on this tawny steed to go forth—
the well-armed, most intoxicating one. This very bull, the chariot, has clothed himself in the woolly fleece of the sheep.
Going toward thousandfold booty... The maidens of Trita urge this tawny one with the stones—
the drop for Indra to drink.
Like a falcon among the human clans, he settles here;
like a lover going to his mistress, he comes. This exhilarating juice, the child of heaven, looks down from above.
4.5.2.04. He who, as Indu, has entered the filter...

Ten active fingers cleanse this very one, the tawny steed,
with which he adorns himself for exhilaration. This vigorous courser, urged by men, is the lord of all-knowing thought.
He rushes through the sheep’s wool filter. This Soma, pressed for the gods, has flowed into the strainer;
entering all the stations.
This immortal god shines forth upon his station;
he is the slayer of Vṛtra, the one most beloved by the gods. This bull, bellowing loudly, is guided by his ten sisters.
He rushes toward the wooden vats;
this exhilarating, intoxicating draught, purifying itself upon the sky, has caused the sun to shine.
Clothed in light, he shines with the sun, Vivasvat;
the Lord of Speech, the undeceivable one.
This seer, highly praised, pours forth upon the filter.
Being purified, he strikes away our enemies; this one,
winning the light for Indra and Vāyu,
is poured out into the filter, accomplishing skillful power.
This bull, the head of heaven, pressed by men, is led forth; Soma, the knower of all, dwells within the wooden vessels. Seeking cattle and seeking gold, he roars as he flows clear.
The Indu, ever-conquering and unsubdued...
This vigorous, tawny bull has flowed within the mid-air; being purified, the Indu goes toward Indra...
This vigorous Soma, invincible, flows while being purified; he is the one who favors the gods and slays the wicked.
Pressed for the draught, that bull-like Soma flows through the filter.
The god-seeking one wards off obstacles and demons;
he, the far-seeing, the tawny, the sustainer, flows through the filter,
bellowing toward his place of rest.
That steed, Pavamāna, rushes through the luminous realms of heaven;
the slayer of demons, he flows through the woolly filter. On the high ridge of Trita’s dwelling, Pavamāna has caused the light to shine.
Together with his kinsmen, [he reached] the sun...
He is the slayer of Vṛtra, the bull, the pressed one, the finder of wide space, the invincible; Soma has sped forth like toward booty.
That god, impelled by the seer, rushes toward the wooden vats; Indu flows for Indra, bestowing great wealth.
He who studies the *pāvamānī* verses—the essence gathered by the seers—[attains this].
He eats everything purified and made savory by Mātariśvan— Whoever studies the Pāvamānī verses, that essence gathered by the Ṛṣis;
For him Sarasvatī milks forth milk, clarified butter, honey, and water.
The *pāvamānī* verses are auspicious, yielding easily, and dripping with clarity;
they are the essence gathered by the seers, and immortality is placed within the *brāhmaṇas*.
May the *pāvamānī* verses establish us in this world and also in that one beyond.
May the goddesses, brought together with the gods, fulfill our desires.
(1301) With that purifier by which the gods always purify themselves—may the *pāvamānī* verses purify us with that [purifier] of a thousand streams. (1302)
The *pāvamānī* verses bring auspiciousness; by means of them, one goes to the Nandana grove.
One partakes of holy foods and attains immortality.
We have approached with great reverence the Most Youthful One, who has shone forth, well-kindled, in his own dwelling.
Between the two wide worlds, Citrabhānu, well-invoked on all sides and facing every direction...
He, Agni Jātavedas, by his greatness overcoming all difficulties, is to be praised in the house.
May he protect us from misfortune and reproach, and protect us, as well as our patrons, who sing his praises.
O Agni, you are Varuṇa and Mitra; the Vasiṣṭhas magnify you with their hymns.
May all treasures be easy for us to win through you. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
Great is Indra by his might, like Parjanya rich in rain.
4 5 2 10 01c He has grown strong through the hymns of Vatsa...

When the bearers, the inspired singers, bring forth the immortal offspring of the *ṛta*,
they do so with the vehicle of the *ṛta*.
Of the purifying, slaying tawny one, the golden drops have been poured forth.

4 5 2 11 01c The swift ones with unaging radiance... 1310 4 5 2 11 02a Pavamāna, the best of charioteers, most beautifully praised by the beautiful ones; 4 5 2 11 02c golden-hued, he is the host of Maruts. 1311
O Pavamāna, best at winning the prize, pervade [the world] with your rays, bestowing great heroic power upon the singer.
Pour out the pressed Soma on every side; it is the most excellent oblation.

He who, manly, having flowed within the waters, has pressed the Soma with the stones—now, being purified by the sheep’s wool, flow around, unassailable and most fragrant. Even when pressed in the waters, we rejoice in the exhilarating juice; mixing it further with the products of the cow.
4 5 2 12 03a Being pressed for all to see, the exhilarating god, the wise Indu, the inspired one...
1315 4 5 2 13 01a Soma has been pressed, the ruddy bull, the tawny one; like a wondrous king, he has bellowed toward the cows.
4 5 2 13 01c Purifying himself, he passes through the sheep’s wool filter; like a hawk, he has settled in his ghee-filled dwelling. 1316

Parjanya is the father of the great-winged bird; he has established his dwelling upon the mountains at the navel of the earth. The sister waters have flowed forth toward the cows; he clothes himself in the pressing-stones when the sacrifice is prepared.
As a sage, you seek greatness through your skillful wisdom; like a groomed steed, you rush toward the prize.
Driving away misfortunes, O Soma, be gracious to us; clothed in clarity, you go about your radiant garment.
As if rising toward the sun, may all partake of Indra’s bounty. Having been born with power over all generations, we look forward to our portion as our inheritance.
Praise the one who bestows wealth, the giver of bounty; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
He does not frustrate the desire of the worshipper, but impels his mind toward generosity.
O Indra, from whatever we fear, from that do thou protect us.
O Maghavan, grant us that [gift] for our protection; strike away the haters, strike away the adversaries.
(1321) For you, O Lord of Wealth, are the bestower of great riches and the sustainer of the dwelling.
Therefore, O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, we, having pressed the Soma, call upon you. (1322)

O Soma, you are the sustainer, the delightful and most powerful at the sacrifice; flow on, bestowing abundant wealth. You, when pressed, are the most intoxicating, flowing as the one who most exhilarates.
4 5 2 16 02c Indu, the ever-conquering, the unconquered...
1324 4 5 2 16 03a Pressed out by the stones, flow hither, bellowing aloud;
4 5 2 16 03c Bring us brilliant strength! 1325
Flow with your streams in your might for the feast of the gods, O Indu;
as the honeyed Soma, take your seat in our beaker.
Your drops, floating upon the waters, have strengthened Indra for exhilaration.

The immortal gods drank you for immortality. O pressed drops of Soma, being purified, flow toward us with wealth— ye who cause rain from heaven, who release the waters, and who find the light of heaven.
They purify him with the fleece— the beloved, golden-hued, and tawny one—
who goes forth with exhilarating juice to all the gods.
Him, the self-glorious one, whom the two fives [the ten fingers] and his friends press with the stones.
The waves, bathing Indra’s beloved and desirable [Soma], flow forth. O Soma, you are poured out for Indra to drink, for the slayer of Vṛtra;
you are poured for the hero who possesses sacrificial gifts, for the one who sits upon his seat.
Flow on, O Soma, for great skill, like a washed steed, a prize-winner, for the sake of wealth.
The pressers purify your juice for exhilaration; they cleanse the Soma for great splendor.
They groom the infant, the tawny, the drop—Soma—for the gods as he is born in the filter.

O Dawn, the gods have approached the Indu— the newly born, the one who crosses the waters, the breaker [of obstacles], adorned with milk— as they would a calf with nursing mothers. May our songs increase him, as cows nurture their young.

4.5.2.20.02c He who wins the heart of Indra... 1336 4.5.2.20.03a Flow for us, O Soma, for the welfare of our cattle; milk out for us swelling nourishment. 4.5.2.20.03c Increase the ocean that is worthy of praise. 1337
4.5.2.21.01a Those who kindle Agni and spread the sacrificial grass in due order, 4.5.2.21.01c they whose friend is the youthful Indra...
4.5.2.21.02a High indeed is their fuel, abundant their recitation, and wide their sacrificial post.
Those whose youthful Indra is their friend...
1339 Even without fighting, the hero drives away those who have surrounded him with weapons, together with his warriors—those whose youthful Indra is their friend... 1340
He alone who bestows wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations—
Indra, the sovereign and unopposed, is truly [the lord]. For whoever, having pressed the soma, seeks to win you over from among many...
Fierce indeed is that power; Indra alone possesses it. (1342) When will he trample the miserly mortal underfoot, like a mushroom?
When will Indra hear our songs? Indeed, [he possesses it]. (1343)
The singers of the *gāyatrī* chant for you; the reciters of the *ṛk* hymns praise your song.
O Śatakratu, the Brahmans have raised you up like a pillar. When you have ascended from ridge to ridge, you have manifested many deeds to be accomplished.
Indra perceives this purpose; the bull stirs with his herd.
Yoke, O Indra, your two long-maned bay steeds, the vigorous ones that fill out the girths. Then, O Soma-drinker, come to us at the hearing of our songs.
Sixth Chapter. First Half. 4.6.1.01a Well-kindled, O Agni, bring the gods hither for us who offer the oblation. 4.6.1.01c O Purifier, as the Hotṛ priest, perform the sacrifice. 1347
O Sage Tanūnapāt, make our sacrifice rich in sweetness among the gods today for our invocation. I invoke here the beloved Narāśaṃsa at this sacrifice.
O Agni, honey-tongued, prepared with oblations... O Agni, on your most comfortable chariot, being praised, bring the gods here;
you are the Hotṛ-priest appointed by Manu.
Now that the sun has risen today, may Mitra, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Bhaga impel us toward sinlessness. May that dwelling be well-protected; O bounteous ones, lead us forward on our journey.
4.6.1.02. Those who carry us across distress... 4.6.1.03. And those self-ruling ones, Aditi, and those who [uphold] the unimpaired vow— The great kings who rule over it.
May the Soma juices gladden you; bestow bounty, O wielder of the stone!
Strike down those who hate the sacred word.
Trample with your foot the stingy Panis; you are great.
For there is no one at all who can oppose you;
you, O Indra, are the lord of the pressed juices and of the unpressed.
You are the king of the people.
The watchful sage of holy thoughts, Soma, being purified, has settled within the vessels.
Him the pairs of Adhvaryus, longing for him, serve—the charioteers with skillful hands. Being purified, bestowing gifts upon the sun, he has filled both worlds; he has shone them wide apart.
Even he whose dear ones are dear for his aid, being present, shall not withhold wealth from the one who performs the rite.

He, the increaser and the strengthener, being purified, Soma the bounteous, has protected us with light— wherein our ancient fathers, knowers of the path and finders of heaven, struck the rock for the sake of the cows.
4.6.1.05.01a Do not praise anything else at all; O friends, do not suffer harm.
4.6.1.05.01c Praise Indra alone, the bull, when the soma is pressed; recite your hymns repeatedly.
4.6.1.05.02a [Praise him who is] like a rushing bull that tramples down, like a cow, the subduer of men.

The incantation for causing enmity, the incantation for winning over, that which effects both, most bountiful, and bringing about both results. Upward rise these most honey-sweet songs, these hymns of praise, like chariots of the victorious, winners of wealth, possessing inexhaustible aid, and full of vigor.
Like the Kaṇvas, like the Bhr̥gus, like the Suns, they have attained all that is to be desired. Exalting Indra with hymns, the Āyus and the Priyamedhas have raised their voices.
Now run forth indeed for the winning of booty; as one who overcomes obstacles, go around the Vritras.
4.6.1.07.01cd: You hasten toward us like one seeking to cross over enemies or pay off debts.
4.6.1.07.02ab: For you, O Pavamāna, have generated the sun and, through your power, the milk for its support. 4.6.1.07.02cd: Rushing forward with the wisdom that quickens the kine.
For we rejoice in you, O Soma, once you are pressed, for the sake of great sovereignty over the assembly. O Pavamāna, you plunge forward toward the spoils of war.
Flow forth, O Soma, as a sweet draught for Indra, for Mitra, for Pūṣan, and for Bhaga.
Thus flow for the sake of immortality and the great dwelling; flow, O bright celestial nectar. May Indra drink of your pressed Soma for wisdom and skill, and may all the gods do likewise.
Like the rays of the sun, the exhilarating, flowing drops rush forth together.
The swift streams flow around the stretched-out thread; there is no domain that flows without Indra.
The thought is joined to him, honey is poured out; the sweet-tongued one is urged within the mouth.
Pavamāna, like the continuous stream of those who press the juice, the honeyed drop flows through the filter.

The bull bellows; the milch-cows, the goddesses, come toward him; they approach the appointed place of the god. Soma has passed through the white sheep’s wool; like a washed garment, he has clothed himself in it.
Men have generated the praiseworthy Agni from the two fire-sticks with their prayers, as he is set in motion by their hands.

The Vasus established that Agni within the dwelling, him who is visible from afar, unassailable, and beautiful to behold for protection from every side— he who is worthy of skillful service and is the eternal lord of the house.
O Agni, blaze forth for us, most youthful one, with your unaging flame.
To you, O youngest god, all sacrificial strengths constantly flow.
This spotted bull has come; he has settled before his mother.
And going toward his father, the light... he moves within the luminous spheres, breathing out from his breath;
the Great One has looked across the sky.
He shines across thirty realms; speech is bestowed upon the bird.
Day after day, at every dawn, through the days...
[Sixth Prapāṭhaka, Second Half]
Approaching the sacrifice, let us address a prayer to Agni,
who hears us even from afar— Agni who was the foremost among the tribes when they gathered together in their longing.
He protected the household for the donor... He, Agni, the most auspicious, may he protect our wealth and our kin; and may he deliver us from distress.
And let the people say, "Agni, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been born;
the winner of wealth in every battle. O Agni, yoke those horses of yours, O God, which are well-trained.
The swift steeds carry you hither;
come toward us, bring [the gods] to enjoy the offerings, that they may drink the Soma. 1383–1384.
O Agni, descendant of Bharata, shine forth with undecaying splendor; blaze up and radiate, O ageless one!
Like a mortal, he desires that speech for the one who presses the soma-juice.
Drive away the stingy dog; strike him down as the Bhr̥gus struck Makha.
The kinsman has clothed himself in his mantle, like a son for enjoyment between his parents' arms. He has gone forth like a lover to a maiden, like a suitor to sit upon the womb.
That hero, the accomplisher of skill, who has propped apart the two worlds— he, the tawny one, has clothed himself in the filter like a wise ordainer settling into his seat.
O Indra, by your very birth, from of old, you have been without a rival, without kin, and without a friend.
In battle you seek the friendship of the ally; you do not find the wealthy man for companionship. Your horses are contemptuous.
When you make a roar, you gather [the hosts] together, and then you are invoked like a father.

May a thousand and a hundred horses, yoked to your golden chariot— tawny steeds with long manes, harnessed by prayer— bring you, O Indra, for the drinking of Soma. May your two tawny steeds, with tails like peacocks' feathers, bring you upon the golden chariot.
Let the white-backed ones carry [the Soma] for the drinking of the exhilarating, sweet juice.
O lover of songs, drink of this pressed soma as the first drinker;
this well-prepared, flavorful draught is offered as a delightful means for intoxication.
O pressers, pour out the Soma like a horse— a hymn that crosses the waters, traverses the mid-air, fills the woods, and floats upon the waves;
a bull with a thousand streams, milking forth milk, dear to the race of gods.

He who, born of *ṛta*, has grown strong through *ṛta*— the divine King, the lofty *ṛta*. May Agni, desiring wealth, strike down the Vṛtras with his song of praise— he who is kindled, bright, and invoked with offerings.
In the womb of the mother, the father of the father, flashing in the imperishable,
he sits within the womb of Ṛta.
O Jātavedas, you who are far-seeing, bring us a prayer that brings progeny.
O Agni, that which has shone in heaven...

[1398] Being purified by his impulse and his zeal, the god has mingled his juice with the gods. Pressed out, he goes around the filter chanting, like a Hotṛ-priest at the measured dwellings rich in cattle. [1399]
Clothed in auspicious, well-fitting garments, the great sage, reciting his inspired words,
flows into the two bowls while being purified— far-sighted and watchful at the banquet for the gods.
On the sheep’s-wool back, the beloved one is cleansed, the most glorious among the glorious, our ruler.
Resound as you flow, being purified! Do you protect us always with your blessings! (1401) Come now, let us praise Indra, the pure one, with a pure *sāman*;
may he, who has grown strong through pure hymns (*uktha*), be exhilarated by the pure libations accompanied by blessings. (1402)
O Indra, come to us pure, with your pure aids;
being pure, bestow wealth upon us; being pure, O drinker of Soma, rejoice!
For you, O Indra, are pure; as the pure one, grant wealth and treasures to the donor.
Pure, you strike down the Vṛtras; pure, you seek to win the prize of strength.
O Agni, we meditate today upon the effective hymn for you who touch the heavens, we who long for the wealth of the god.
May Agni, who is the Hotṛ among men, enjoy our songs;
may he worship the divine host. O Agni, you are far-extending, the beloved and most excellent Hotṛ.
By you they extend the sacrifice...
(1407) The voices have lowed toward the three-backed bull, the bestower of vital strength, the one who seeks the light.
Dwelling in the woods like Varuṇa among the rivers, the bestower of jewels distributes desirable treasures. (1408)
O hero of the host, possessing all valour, victorious, powerful, the winner of riches—flow on!
Armed with sharp weapons, swift with the bow, invincible in battles, overcoming enemies in the fray—flow on! Creating wide pastures and security, bringing together the two worlds of wisdom, flow on!
Desiring to win the waters, the dawns, and the heavenly realms, he has bellowed together for us great spoils of war.
O Indra, you are glorious, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, the lord of power.
You alone slay the Vṛtras that are irresistible; you are the one who is not to be turned back, the sustainer of the people.
We now entreat you, O Asura, the wise one, for wealth as our allotted share.
Like a great, protective skin, O Indra, may your favors reach us.
We have chosen you, the best of sacrificers, the immortal god among gods, as the Hotṛ-priest.
Of this sacrifice, [he is] the skillful performer... The Son of the Waters, the fortunate one, the brightly shining Agni of most excellent luster—
may he, as the friend of Mitra and Varuṇa, and as the friend of the Waters, worship for us [their] favor in heaven.
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on toward spoils— he shall be the master of eternal refreshments. O Conqueror,
no one at all can overcome him, whoever he may be.
There is a prize worthy of renown;
may he, who is observed by all people, be a conqueror with his steeds; may he be a winner with the inspired singers.

The ten sisters, the flowing prayers of the wise one, together cleanse the Soma as it is sprinkled. The golden-hued one has run forth from the offspring of the Sun; like a prize-winning steed, he has reached the wooden vat.
Like a lowing infant with its mothers, the bull, rich in boons, has flowed along with the waters.
Like a young man going to a tryst with a maiden, he goes to the jar to unite with the milk-cows.
And the udder of the cow has swelled; the wise Indu accompanies her with his streams. The cows mix him, the head, with milk in the vessels, as if with freshly washed treasures.
Drink of the flavorful pressed juice; O Indra, intoxicate yourself with our soma mixed with milk.
Be our kinsman at the shared feast for our prosperity; may your insights protect us.
May we, as prize-winners, remain in your favor; do not abandon us to the enemy.
Protect us with your wondrous aids; lead us toward your favors.
For him, the thrice-seven milch-cows have yielded the true milk-mixture in the highest heaven.
He has fashioned four other beautiful worlds for his adornment, when he grew strong through the eternal laws.
Consuming the lovely nectar of immortality, he has by his poetic wisdom separated both heaven and earth.
He has clothed himself in most brilliant waters with majesty, when they have found his seat through the glory of the god.
May those rays of his be immortal and invincible, following after both generations.
By those [means] through which they purify both human and divine powers, the sages have seized the King from the very beginning.
1425 Flow forth to Vāyu for his enjoyment, being praised; flow purified toward Mitra and Varuṇa.
1426 Flow toward the hero who quickens the prayer and stands upon the chariot; flow toward Indra, the bull with the thunderbolt in his arm. 1426
Flow toward us with well-woven garments; being purified, flow toward us with cows that yield milk easily. O divine Soma, bring to us bright gold for our wearing, and horses with chariots.
Flow toward us, being purified, bringing celestial treasures and all earthly riches.
By which we may obtain wealth and the status of a seer, as Jamadagni did for us. When you were born, O matchless Maghavan, for the slaying of Vṛtra,
then you spread out the earth and propped up the heavens.
From that the sacrifice was born, from that the hymn and the joyful song;
you are the all-surpassing one over all that is born and all that is to be born.
You placed the cooked food within the raw cows and made the sun ascend in heaven.
Heat us with your song like the *gharma* vessel, O you who are beloved by those who delight in hymns, with great and well-fashioned praises.
(1431) O Lord of the Bay Horses, your exhilarating, intoxicating draught is for you to drink, as if from a great vessel.
O Bull, your bull-like *indu* is a prize-winning steed that wins a thousandfold. (1432)

O Indra, let the exhilarating, excellent, and bull-like intoxication come to us; it is victorious, winning, and the immortal subduer of armies. For you, O hero, are the winner; you urge on the chariot of man.
4.6.2 (2003c) O companion, burn away the Dasyu who lacks holy vows, as one burns a vessel with flame.
[End of] the sixth prapāṭhaka, third half.
4.6.3 (0101a) Flow for us, bringing rain; bring down the wave of the waters from heaven.
Free from disease, providing abundant nourishment—
flow with that stream by which the cattle of the people may come here to our house.
Flow with your stream as clarified butter, most beloved by the gods at the sacrifices;
flow for us, bringing rain.
Flow through the filter with your stream for our nourishment, spreading far and wide.
May the gods indeed hear us.
Pavamāna has flowed forth; he has struck down the demons. Illuminating the lights as of old, he shines.
Bring all things to him who desires to drink, who knows everything,
who comes readily, who moves swiftly, and whose path is never behind others,
O men! Come toward him with Soma juices— he is the greatest drinker of Soma.
With vessels, with pressed drops, [we worship] Indra, the possessor of the *ṛjīṣa*.
(1441) When you honor him with pressed drops, with Soma juices, the wise one knows all; the bold one seeks out that thread. (1442)
O Adhvaryu, bring forth this pressed juice for him, for him alone.
Will he not perhaps ward off the curse of that arrogant, noble-born man?
Now, for the tawny one, who is self-strong, ruddy, and touches the heavens—
Sing a song of praise to Soma.
Purify the pressed Soma with stones held in the hands;
pour forth the honey into the honey.
Sit down with reverence; mix [the soma] with curds.
Place the drop within Indra.
O Soma, slayer of enemies, most observant, flow pure for the welfare of our cattle.
O Soma, you who fulfill the desires of the gods, you are poured out for Indra to drink, for his exhilaration. O Lord of the mind, you are the one whose essence is thought.
O Pavamāna Soma, bestow upon us wealth and heroic strength;
O Indu, with Indra as our ally...
[raise up] the one of renowned bounty, the bull, whose deeds are manly.
O Sūrya, you go forth across the eight directions. He who by the strength of his arms shattered ninety-nine fortresses, that slayer of Vṛtra, has slain Ahi.
May that Indra be our auspicious friend; may he yield for us horses, cattle, and barley, like a wide-streaming cow.
May the radiant, exalted one drink the Soma-mead, bestowing unimpaired life upon the lord of the sacrifice.

Impelled by the wind, he who protects by his own power fulfills all creatures and shines forth in many ways. Vibhrāḍ! The great, well-sustained, most excellent winner of booty, the law of heaven established upon its foundation, the truth—this light has been born, the slayer of enemies, the slayer of Vṛtra, the greatest slayer of Dasyus, the slayer of Asuras, the slayer of rivals.
This is the best of lights, the supreme light; it is called the all-conquering, the wealth-winning, the Great.
All-shining, a great radiance, Sūrya has spread wide for us to see—his power is vast and unshakable.
O Indra, bring us mental power, as a father provides for his sons.
O you who are invoked by many, grant us instruction on this path; may we attain the light of life. (1456) Let not unknown, malevolent, or unpropitious powers step upon us.
O Hero, with your aid, may we cross over the ever-flowing waters and the steep descents. (1457)
O Indra, protect us today and every day, tomorrow and every tomorrow, and in the days to come.
O Lord of the Good, you shall guard all our singers throughout the days, by day and by night.
The breaker of foes, the hero, the bountiful Maghavan, rich in wealth, is ever ready for heroic deeds.
Both your arms are virile, O Śatakratu, those which have grasped the thunderbolt.
Desiring wives, indeed, and desiring sons, we invoke Sarasvant, O bounteous ones.
And may Sarasvatī, who is dear among the dear, who has seven sisters, and who is well-beloved, be worthy of our praise.
We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ.
May he who shall impel our thoughts [be seated]...
O Brahmaṇaspati, make us a resonator of the Soma-pressings,
as Kakṣīvat was for Auśija.
O Agni, you purify our lives; send us strength and nourishment. Drive far away misfortune.
May those [powers] of yours enable us to obtain great earthly and celestial wealth.
Great indeed is their sovereignty among the gods;
they honor the eternal Law with the eternal Law, and they have attained vigorous skill. Free from malice, the two gods prosper.
4.6.3.1103a Vṛṣṭidyāvā and Rītyāp, the lords of the gift, [bestowed] the Dānumatī.
4.6.3.1103c They have reached the great pit.
4.6.3.1201a They yoke the ruddy, bright one as he moves around those who stand still.
The luminaries shine in heaven... They yoke his two beloved bay horses to the chariot on either side—
the ruddy, bold steeds that carry the hero.
Making a banner for the bannerless, O men, a form for the formless, you were born together with the dawns.
This Soma, O Indra, is pressed for you; for you it purifies itself; drink of it.

For you indeed have prepared it; you have poured out the drop, the Soma, for the exhilarating draught that is yours. Like a chariot capable of bearing much, he has been harnessed for the winning of many great treasures.
Then all the human races and the trees cried out upward in the contest for the light.

4.6.3.1303a Flow onward, powerful as the host of Maruts, like the divine folk who are beyond reproach. 4.6.3.1303c Like waters, be swift with favor toward us; like a sacrifice, you possess a thousandfold power and conquer in battle.
4.6.3.1401a O Agni, you have been appointed as the Hotṛ-priest of all sacrifices.
With the gods among the human folk...
with our delightful tongues at the sacrifice, do thou worship the Great One. Bring hither the gods and offer them sacrifice.
For you, O wise one, know the ways and paths to the gods directly,
O Agni of noble intellect in the sacrifices.
The immortal god, the Hotṛ-priest, goes before us with his creative power.
Impelling the assemblies of knowledge...
the vigorous steed is placed in the contests for booty; he is led forward in the sacrificial rites, the inspired sage who accomplishes the sacrifice.

By his wisdom, the one worthy of choice made [the world]; he received the germ of beings, the father of Dakṣa, through his own body. Pour forth splendor upon the pressed juice, the glory that overspreads heaven and earth.
The juices shall hold the bull...
They know their own dwelling-place; like calves with their mothers, they meet together with their kin.
4.6.3.1603a: Devouring within the jaws, they create a support in heaven;
to Indra and Agni, homage! Light! 4.6.3.1701a:
That indeed was the eldest among all beings, from which was born the fierce one, of brilliant valor.
As soon as he is born, he strikes down his enemies—he whom all the helpers rejoice in.
Increasing in power, possessing abundant strength, he, the foe, instills fear in the Dāsa. Winning both the unyielding and the yielding, they cry out to you at the offerings during the exhilarations.
All turn their will toward you when these helpers become twice or thrice [in number].

Mix the sweeter with the sweet; fight well with honey against honey. At the Trikadruka sacrifices, the mighty and very vigorous buffalo drank the barley-mixed Soma pressed by Viṣṇu, according to his desire, until he was satiated.
He has exhilarated him for the performance of great deeds; he, the great and wide one, has followed him. The true *indu* (Soma-drop), a god, has followed the god, the true *indu*, the true Indra.
Born together with wisdom, you have grown together with power; grown together with heroic deeds, you are the overcomer of adversaries, O far-seeing one.
You are the giver of wealth and desirable riches to the one who praises you, O wise one. He, the true *indu*, a god, has followed the god, the true *indu*, the true Indra.
Then, radiant with brilliance, he overcame Krivi by his might in battle; he filled the two worlds, heaven and earth, with his majesty and grew even greater.
He placed one [portion] within his belly, while the other overflowed. Awaken him! May the god accompany the god; may the true *indu* (Soma-drop) attend the true Indra.
Seventh Chapter. First Half.
Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, as he is known:
the son of truth, the protector of the righteous.
The bay steeds have been let loose upon the red sacrificial grass.
Wherein we rejoice together—
there for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows have yielded the milk-mixture, the honey-sweet draught,
when he found it in his secret hiding place.
Adorn Indra for us in all battles as one to be invoked;
come to our prayers and libations, O Vṛtra-slayer, supreme victor, worthy of praise!
You are the foremost giver of riches, you are the true one who acts with sovereign power.
We choose the alliance of the greatly resplendent one, of the great son of strength.
From the great depth of heaven, they have milked out the ancient, primordial, and praiseworthy nectar;
they raised a chorus together for Indra as he was being born.
Beholding the primordial source, those who shine with wealth have sung forth to the divine waters;
Savitṛ unbars the door of heaven as it were.
And now, O Pavamāna, when you encompass these two worlds, heaven and earth, and all these beings with your might.
Like a bull among the herd, you shine forth as sovereign lord.
O Agni, proclaim this our newest song of praise to the gods, that we may obtain gain.
O Citrabhānu, you are distributed even near the wave of the Sindhu;
instantly you flow for the donor. Grant us a share in the highest and the middle spoils of war.
I have learned the instruction of the nearest treasure. Indeed, from my father I received the wisdom of the immortal;
I was born like the sun.
Through my ancient birth, I adorn my songs like Kaṇva, by which Indra indeed gains his strength. Those ṛṣis who have not praised you, O Indra, and those who have praised you— [all of them...]

O Agni, well-praised, increase my [glory]. O Agni, created by strength, take pleasure in our prayer together with all the fires—those that are among the gods and those that are among men; through them, magnify our songs of praise.
May that Agni, together with all the Agnis, [be present] for him who possesses the prize-winning steed; may he, surrounded by strengths, be well-disposed toward our offspring and descendants.
