I invoke the two exhilarating slayers of Vṛtra, the victorious and unconquered ones,
Indra and Agni, the greatest winners of booty. The chanters who know the hymns and the ways of praise sing forth to you both.
4.8.2 1702c I invoke Indra and Agni for nourishment...
1703 4.8.2 1703a O Indra and Agni, you shook down the ninety forts belonging to the Dāsas, 4.8.2 1703c all at once by a single deed... 1704

O Agni, son of strength, we who offer nourishment have poured forth our songs toward you, whose appearance is delightful. Like seeking shade from the heat of the sun, we have come for refuge under your protection.
O Agni, you who have the luster of gold... [1706] Like a fierce archer, like a bull with sharpened horns, O Agni, you have shattered the fortresses. [1707]
We pray for the eternal Gharma, the upholder of Truth, Vaiśvānara, the Lord of the light of Truth. He who has spread himself out here, crossing over to the heavenly light of the sacrifice.
The self-controlled one releases the seasons;
Agni, in his beloved abodes, is the desire of all that has been and is yet to be. Shining as the sole sovereign, he rules over all.
Eighth Prapāṭhaka, Third Half:
4.8.3. Agni, beautifying his own body through his ancient birth, the Seer has grown great by means of the inspired singer. 1711.
I invoke the Son of Strength, Agni, with his purifying flame,
at this well-performed sacrifice.
O Agni, great as Mitra, do thou [favor us] with thy bright radiance.
Sit upon the sacrificial grass with the gods.
O wielder of the stone, your vital powers have risen up, shattering the demons; drive away those who are our rivals.
With this [power] you have struck down [the foe] by your might when chariots clash and wealth is staked;
praise him with a fearless heart. No one can violate the laws of this Pavamāna through evil intent.
4.8.3 "O you who cause pain to him who attacks you...
1716 4.8.3 "They drive forth the exhilarating, tawny, prize-winning steed into the rivers—the Indu, the intoxicant for Indra. 1717
Come, O Indra, with your joyous bay horses whose hair is like peacock feathers. Let no one, not even those with snares, restrain you; pass over them as if across a desert.
You are the devourer of Vṛtra, the breaker of Vala, the destroyer of forts, and the driver-forth of the waters.

Indra is the driver of the chariot and the master of the two bay horses; he shatters even the firmest things. Like deep-sea oceans, you nourish your mental power (*kratu*); like cows, you let loose your songs.
Well-guarded, they have reached him as milch-cows seek pasture, as streams flow into a lake.
Just as a thirsty buffalo goes from the water to a dry place, so come quickly to us at our approach and our departure; drink well among the Kaṇvas.
O Maghavan Indra, may these drops exhilarate you for the sake of bestowing wealth upon the one who presses the juice.
From that [pressing], you drank the Soma juice extracted in the *camū* vessel; therein you have established your supreme might.
O most powerful God, you indeed praise the mortal man;
O Maghavan Indra, there is no one other than you who is a comforter—this word I speak to you.
O Vasu, let not your bounties nor your aids ever deceive us.
O Manu’s son, bestow upon us all human riches for the sake of our people. This noble lady, shining forth, has come from her sister.
The daughter of Heaven has been seen;
like a dappled mare, ruddy and rich in milk, she is the mother of the cows, the observer of the eternal law (*ṛta*). Dawn has become the friend of the Aśvins.
You are indeed the friend of the Aśvins, and you are the mother of the cows;
O Uṣas, you rule over wealth. This unprecedented Uṣas, the beloved of heaven, now shines forth.
I praise you both, O Aśvins, with a lofty hymn— you two wonder-workers, sons of Sindhu, discoverers of riches,
gods who find wealth through our prayer.
Your towering steeds shall be proclaimed upon the surface of the ancient earth,
when your chariot flies with its winged birds. O Dawn, rich in prizes, bring that wondrous wealth to us.
By which we may maintain both our children and our progeny... O Uṣas, rich in cattle and horses, radiant one, shine forth here today for us, bringing wealth and abundance, O you who are full of joy!
Yoke, O Uṣas rich in steeds, your ruddy horses today; then bring to us all auspicious fortunes.
O Aśvins, wonder-workers, come to our dwelling, bringing cattle and gold.
With one mind, direct the chariot hitherward.
O gods, the wonder-workers who bring bliss, whose paths are golden— may those who awaken at dawn bring you here for the drinking of Soma.
As far as this verse reaches, you two have created light for the people from heaven. O Aśvins, bring nourishment to us!
I think of that Agni who is the Vasu, to whom the milch-cows go.
May the swift steeds come hither; may the constant, powerful ones come. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
For Agni, the lord of all people, bestows a prize-winning steed upon the clan.
Agni grants wealth that is self-sustaining; being well-pleased, he goes toward what is desirable. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
He is Agni who is praised as the Vasu, unto whom the milch-cows come together, and the swift-running steeds, and the well-born patrons; bring nourishment to those who praise thee!
O Uṣas, radiant one, awaken us today for great wealth.
Just as you awakened us for Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born Dawn, rich in horses and bounty;
O Daughter of Heaven, who have shone forth for Sunītha Śaucadratha— so shine forth for the more powerful Satyaśravas Vāyya, O well-born Dawn, rich in horses and bounty.
May she who brings us wealth dawn for us today, O daughter of heaven!
You who have shone forth upon Sahīyas, Satyaśravas, Yāyya, Sujāta, and Aśvasūnṛta.
[I praise] the most beloved chariot, the powerful one that carries riches.

The seer, your praiser, O Aśvins, adorns you with hymns; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call! Come forth, O Aśvins, beyond all people, through the ancient [paths], O wonder-workers who travel on golden paths, who are full of bliss, and who are borne by the rivers; O lovers of sweetness, hear my call!
O Aśvins, come to us bearing treasures;
you two Rudras who travel on golden paths, you who possess wealth in horses, lovers of sweetness, hear my invocation with favor.
Agni has been awakened by the fuel of the people, facing the Dawn as she approaches like a milch-cow.
Like young birds springing up to the branches, his rays stream forth toward the firmament.
The Hotṛ-priest has been awakened for the sacrifice to the gods; Agni, well-disposed, has stood upright at dawn.
As he is kindled, his radiant splendor is seen; the great god has been released from the darkness.

When he has awakened the tether of the host, the pure Agni anoints himself with pure rays of light. The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), seeking booty, is harnessed; standing upright, he has sucked the outstretched [udder] with his ladles. This most excellent light among lights has come; the bright, far-reaching signal has been born.

Just as she was impelled for the impulse of Savitṛ, so has Night yielded her womb to Dawn. 1749 The bright one has come with her shining calf; the white one has arrived, and the black one has departed from her dwellings.
Of common kinship, immortal, following one after the other, the two heavens move along, wearing away their color. 1750

Common is the path of the two sisters, endless; they travel it one after the other, instructed by the gods. They do not clash, nor do they stand still; well-established, Night and Dawn are of one mind though different in form.
Agni shines forth at the face of the Dawns; the god-seeking voices of the sages have arisen.
O Aśvins, come hither now on your chariot toward this overflowing draught of warm milk.
You two, who go most readily to what is prepared, are surely here at our praise.
At the arrival of day, you are the swiftest to come with your aid; you are the most beneficent for the donor who turns toward you.
And come at the time of gathering, at the morning of the day, at midday, and at the rising of the sun;
by day and by night with most peaceful aid, O Aśvins, let not the drinking now be delayed for you.
These very Dawns have made their signal; in the eastern half of the firmament they spread their light.
Like bold men fashioning their weapons, the ruddy cows, the mothers, come forth.
1755 The ruddy beams have flown up at will; they have yoked the self-yoking ruddy cows. The dawns have performed their works as of old; the ruddy ones have established their radiant light. 1756
The active women sing with their labors, traveling together from afar by a common path.
Bringing nourishment to the well-doing, bounteous giver, they come every day for the sake of the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Agni has been awakened; the sun rises from the earth; the radiant, great dawns have shone forth with their light.
The Aśvins have yoked their chariot to travel; the god Savitṛ has impelled the world apart.
O Aśvins, when you yoke your bull-like chariot, sprinkle our dominion with ghee and honey. Strengthen our prayer in battles; may we share in the spoils in the contest for wealth.
May the three-wheeled chariot of the Aśvins, carrying honey, drawn by swift horses, and well-praised, come hither.
May that three-seated, wealthy chariot, bringing all prosperity, bring welfare to our bipeds and quadrupeds.
Your unceasing streams flow forth like rains from heaven.
Toward thousandfold booty...
Beholding all dear poetic insights, he flows forth;
the tawny one, brandishing his weapons...
Grooming himself with the Āyus, like a king who observes his vows,
he sits among the woods like a hawk;
may he [bring] all treasures for us from heaven and from the earth.
4.8.3.1804c: O Indu, being purified, bring [the wealth]...
1764. Ninth Prapāṭhaka. First Half.
4.9.1.0101a: His streams have flowed forth with the vigor of the pressed-out bull.
The two who prevail over the gods...
the wise ones groom the steed, chanting with song, O poets— the light that has been born, worthy of praise.
O Soma, Lord of abundant wealth, these things are easy for you to endure as you are being purified; increase the ocean that is worthy of praise.
This is the priest who is timely; he is celebrated by the name Indra, and I laud him.

O Lord of Might, our songs go forth to you like harnessed teams; O Indra, let your gifts flow forth like streams upon their paths. We turn you toward us for our protection and for our favor, as one turns a chariot.

Indra, the most powerful lord of the virtuous, who performs great deeds and overcomes the assault of death— O you of mighty strength, of many powers, and of great wisdom, you have filled [the world] with your greatness through every thought.
By whose greatness, O Mighty One, your two hands have reached around the earth as it moves, grasping the golden thunderbolt.
He who has shone upon the city Nārmiṇī, like a transcendent seer, like a steed of the clouds.
Like the sun, shining with a hundredfold self...
The twice-born one, blazing forth, has taken his place over the three luminous realms and all the regions;
the most excellent sacrificer, the Hotṛ-priest, in the gathering place of the waters.
This is that Hotṛ priest, the twice-born, who bestows all desirable things out of a desire for glory—he, the mortal, who has offered oblations to him with well-prepared gifts.
O Agni, today [favor] him with hymns, like a horse; [grant him] auspicious will that touches the heart.
May we succeed through your offerings. For now, O Agni, you have become the charioteer of auspicious will, of skillful and effective power, and of the great cosmic order (*ṛta*).
Through these our hymns, O Agni, turn toward us; O immortal one, with all your radiant faces, be well-disposed toward us like the light of heaven.
O immortal Agni, [grant] the wonderful bounty of the dawning dawn.
O Jātavedas, bring today to the donor the gods who awaken at dawn.
For you are the beloved messenger, the carrier of oblations, O Agni, the charioteer of the sacrifices.
In harmony with the Aśvins and Uṣas, bestow upon us great heroic strength and high renown.
The gray-haired one has swallowed the moon as it sped in the assembly of many, though it was still young.
Behold the poetic power of the god through his greatness: he who was here yesterday has died today.
By his own might, the mighty, ruddy, fair-winged one—the great hero who from of old has no nest—has come forth.
Whatever he has willed is indeed true and not in vain; he is the winner and giver of desirable wealth.
Through these [powers] the wielder of the thunderbolt obtained manly strengths and virilities, by which he grew mighty for the slaying of Vṛtra.
Those gods who, through the greatness of the rite being performed, were born even before the rite itself.
This Soma has been pressed; of it the Maruts drink, and the self-ruling Aśvins as well.
Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa drink of the purified juice continuously.
Of him who dwells in the three abodes and is born of life... And indeed, Indra shall delight in this pressed juice mixed with milk, even as the Hotṛ-priest at dawn.
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great; truly, O Āditya, you are great.
The greatness of you who exist as such is most worthy of praise; by your majesty, O God, you are great.
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great in fame; altogether, O God, you are great.

By his greatness, he is the divine priest of the gods, the lord of asuras; he is the pervasive, invincible light. (1789) Come to our pressed juice with your bay horses, O Lord of exhilarations! Come to our pressed juice with your bay horses! (1790)
He who is doubly the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, Indra, known as the one of a hundred powers— come with your bay steeds to our pressed juice!
For you, O slayer of Vṛtra, are the drinker of these Soma draughts.
Come to our pressed [juice] with your bay horses...
Bring forth [your song] for the great one, who grows great; offer your devotion to the wise one. Go forth to the many clans, O filler of the peoples!
For the far-reaching, mighty Indra, the inspired poets have generated a hymn and a prayer. The wise do not violate his ordinances.
The voices have established Indra as the king, whose wrath is unsurpassed, so that he may prevail forever.
4.9.1.1103c: For Haryaśva, increase the full udders...
1795 4.9.1.1201a: O Indra, if I were the lord of as much wealth as you possess, 4.9.1.1201c: I would surely grant it to the singer; O Dispenser of Wealth, I would not leave him to misery. 1796
Day by day may I learn to magnify you, so that wealth may be found for me from wherever it may be.
For there is no kinship better than yours, O Maghavan, nor is there any father other than you.
Hear the call of the one who has drunk deeply of the stone; take note of the inspired thought of the sage who praises you.
Perform these most intimate acts of worship;
may we be close to you. Knowing them, I do not forget the songs nor the well-spoken praise of you, the swift one, the lordly one; ever I proclaim your name, O self-glorious one.
For many indeed are your libations among men; many a time the wise one calls upon you.
O Maghavan, do not abandon us for long.
Sing forth this strengthening hymn to this Indra, whose chariot is foremost.
Even in the encounter, O creator of space, slayer of Vṛtra in the clash of battles, be our inspirer! May the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows!
You released the rivers to flow downward; you slew the serpent.
O Indra, you were born without an enemy; you nourish every desirable thing.
We embrace you; let the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows.
May all hostilities be utterly dispersed; may the prayers of the noble one reach us.
Cast down the weapon upon the enemy who seeks to slay us, O Indra. May the gift that you bestow as wealth be ours; may the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows.
O wealthy one, may the singer of your praises be prosperous through you, the bountiful lord.
O Lord of the Bay Steeds, partake of the pressed juice...
And the elephant has not noticed the hymn being recited, nor the wealth,
nor the *gāyatra* chant being sung.
O Indra, do not deliver us to the scorner nor to the arrogant;
O possessor of power, aid us with your powers. O Indra, come hither with your bay steeds to the beautiful hymn of Kaṇva.
From the command of that heaven, you two have gone to heaven, O ye who possess the wealth of light.
Here, like a wolf shaking out its entrails, he has shaken off the rims of these [soma-vessels].
From the command of that heaven, you two have gone to heaven, O ye who possess the wealth of light.
May the Soma-pressing stone, speaking here with its roar, bring you hither.
By the command of yonder heaven, go to heaven, O you who are rich in light!
Flow on, O Soma, exhilarating for Indra, most full of sweetness.
These wise, bright drops have been poured forth for Vāyu.
They have been released for the feast of the gods, like chariots seeking booty.
I honor Agni, the Hotṛ, the bounteous giver, the son of strength, Jātavedas—the sage-like Jātavedas.

The god who is upright, whose sacrifice is well-performed, with his form directed toward the gods, following the brilliance of the clarified butter, the white radiance of the offered fat— O inspired singer, we sacrificers invoke you, the best of sacrificers, the eldest of the Aṅgirases, the pure one, with our inspired hymns and with the inspired hymns of the seers.
Like one who traverses the sky, he is the Hotṛ-priest of the peoples—the flame-haired bull whom these clans shall favor for their impulsion, these very clans.
For he, shining with manifold power and radiant luster, becomes the destroyer of the malicious; like an axe, he is the destroyer of the malicious.
Even that which is firm, at his onset, yields like trees when struck; though it stands steady, it submits as if being subdued.
Overpowering, he restrains it; he does not lead it away, for he is a conqueror of the bow.
Ninth Prapāṭhaka. Second Half.
O Agni, yours is fame and vital power; your rays shine brightly, O Vibhāvasu. O Bṛhadbhānu, through your strength you bestow upon the donor praiseworthy booty, O Sage.
With purifying luster, with bright luster, with unimpaired luster, you rise up with your radiance.
O Son, wandering about, you attend upon your two mothers; you fill both worlds.
O Jātavedas, Son of Strength, rejoice in our excellent praises and our prayers, for you are well-disposed toward us.
In you they have gathered their nourishments—those of many forms, with wondrous aids, born of noble lineage.
O Agni, ruling as lord, spread yourself wide with living beings; bestow wealth upon us, O Immortal One!
You shine forth with a form worthy of being beheld; you fulfill the purpose that is well-seen. You are the wise ordainer of the sacrifice, the ruler of great bounty.

You bestow a fortunate gift of beauty, great nourishment, and winning wealth. (1820) For the sake of favor, the people have placed before them Agni—the upholder of *ṛta*, the mighty one, visible to all—him whose ears are quick to hear, the most far-reaching, you, the divine one, through their songs throughout the ages of mankind. (1821)
O Agni, he whom you have protected through friendship overcomes [all] with your aids that bring heroic sons and deeds of strength.
Your dark-blue drop, the lowing one, kindled in due season, has been taken up by the bountiful one.
You are the beloved of the great dawns; you reign over the nights at their break.
1823 The plants have received him as their timely germ; the waters, the mothers, have brought forth Agni.
Him, the very same, the trees and the creepers, both those that bear fruit within and those that do not, bring forth perpetually. 1824
Agni purifies himself for Indra; bright in heaven, he shines forth.
Like a queen, he is born.
He who is awake—the Ṛg-verses desire him; he who is awake—to him the Sāman-chants go.
To him who is awake, this Soma says: "I am yours, dwelling at home in your friendship.
Agni is awake; the Ṛg-verses desire him; Agni is awake; the Sāman-chants go toward him.
To him who is awake, this Soma says: "I am yours, dwelling at home in your friendship."
Homage to my ancient friends; homage to those who sit together.
I yoke the hundred-footed speech;
I yoke the hundred-footed speech, I sing it in its thousand-fold course.
The Gāyatrī,
the Triṣṭubh, and the Jagatī— these all forms were gathered together;
the gods made them their dwellings.
Agni is light, light is Agni; Indra is light, light is Indra;
Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya. Return again with strength, O Agni, with food and long life.
Protect us again from distress; O Agni, return with wealth and swell with a stream that nourishes all,
on every side.
O Indra, if I were the sole lord of wealth as you are,
my praiser would be a friend among cattle.
O Lord of Might, I would bestow upon that wise man and I would desire to give to him.
If I were the lord of cattle...
O Indra, your *sūnṛtā* (generous bounty) is a cow for the sacrificer who presses the soma; swelling with milk, she yields for him both cow and horse.
O Waters, you are indeed the source of bliss; grant us strength for great joy and vision. Grant us a share here of that most auspicious sap which belongs to you.
Like longing mothers, [come] to us... For him for whose dwelling you quicken us, to him let us go gladly; O Waters, give birth to us as well.
May the Wind blow toward us with healing, bringing bliss and joy to our heart;
may he prolong our lives. O Wind, you are indeed our father, and you are our brother and our friend.
Make us live,
O Vāta! That immortal [essence] which is placed in secret in your house over there, O Vāta— grant us a portion of that so that we may live.
The prize-winning steed, possessing all forms, bearing his golden garment and fair wings, has come toward his birthplace;
clothing himself in the radiance of the sun according to the seasons, the swift one has himself generated the sacrificial offering.
The seed of manifold forms was deposited in the waters—that splendor which arose upon the earth.
Measuring out his own greatness in the intermediate space, he neighs loudly; this is the seed of the vigorous horse.
This sacrifice, clothing itself in thousands of yoked [rays], has sustained the splendor of the sun.
Bestower of thousands, giver of hundreds, giver of much, it is the upholder of heaven and the lord of the world.
When they beheld thee with longing in their hearts as thou didst fly toward the vault of heaven like a well-winged bird—
thou of golden wings, the messenger of Varuṇa, the restless bird in the womb of Yama;
then the Gandharva stood erect upon the vault of heaven, bearing his brilliant weapons directed hitherward.
Clothing himself in a fragrant robe, fair to behold, he has generated his own dear names as if out of gold.
When the drop goes toward the ocean, beholding with the eye of a vulture in the expanse of heaven,
the radiant beam, longing with its bright luster, has made its dear abodes in the third realm.
The Ninth Chapter. Third Half.
Swift, sharpening his weapons like a bull, terrible, the striker, the agitator of the people;
the roaring, unblinking, sole hero, Indra, conquered a hundred armies at once. (RV 10.103.1)
With Saṅkrandana, Animiṣa, Jiṣṇu, Yutkara, Duścyavana, and Dhṛṣṇu—with Indra as your ally, O men, conquer in battle and prevail with the Bull who holds arrows in his hand.
He is the master with his band of arrow-handed and quiver-bearing warriors; he is Indra, the uniter in combat.
The conqueror of the gathered host, the drinker of Soma, strong-armed, with a fierce bow,

a shooter with well-aimed arrows— O Bṛhaspati, fly around us on your chariot, slayer of demons, driving away our enemies. Shattering the armies, crushing them in battle, victorious, be the protector of our chariots.

O Indra, victor, powerful, renowned, ancient, preeminent hero, mighty, swift, and conquering, fierce, surpassing heroes, surpassing warriors, born of strength, winner of cattle— mount your victorious chariot! O breaker of enclosures,
winner of cattle, thunderbolt-armed, conquering the race, crushing with your might!
O kinsmen, follow this one; display your heroism! O friends, rally together after Indra!

1854 Piercing the cow-pens with his might, the pitiless hero Indra, whose wrath is a hundredfold—difficult to overthrow, the subduer of armies, the warrior—may he protect our hosts in the battles! 1855

May Indra be their leader; may Bṛhaspati, the sacrificial fee, the sacrifice, and Soma go before them. May the Maruts march at the head of the divine armies as they shatter the foe and achieve victory.
The fierce host of the bull Indra, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts—[may it prevail].
The shout of the high-minded gods, who cause the worlds to tremble, has arisen as they conquer.
O Maghavan, rouse our weapons; rouse the spirits of my warriors.
O Slayer of Vṛtra, let the vigor of the swift steeds be stirred up, and let the shouts of the conquering chariots go forth.
May Indra be with us when the banners meet; may our arrows be victorious.
May our heroes be superior; O gods, protect us in our invocations!
O Maruts, that army of the enemies which approaches us, challenging us in its might—[may it be defeated].
Conceal them with a lawless darkness so that they may not recognize one another.
1860 Bewildering their minds, O *Apvā*, seize their limbs and depart! Advance against them; burn them with sorrows in their hearts; let the enemies be possessed by blinding darkness. 1861
O ghosts, conquer! May Indra grant you protection.
May your arms be fierce so that you may be invincible. Released, fly away, O arrow-shaft sharpened by sacred prayer (*brahman*).
Go to the enemies; fall upon them so that not one of them remains.

Let the *kaṅkas*, the *suparṇas*, and the vultures follow after them; let this army become food for the vultures. Let no one among them escape, nor the one who carries away their wealth; O Indra, let all these birds pursue them.
O Maghavan, against this hostile army that treats us as enemies— O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, let both you and Agni consume it utterly,
where arrows fly together like boys with shorn hair.
May Brahmaṇaspati and Aditi grant us protection there; may they grant us protection for all days.
Drive away the Rakṣas, drive away the adversaries; shatter the jaws of Vṛtra.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, strike down the wrath of the enemy who assails us.
O Indra, strike down our enemies; cast those who attack us low. Whoever seeks to harm us, send him down into the lowest darkness.
The two arms of Indra are powerful and youthful, invincible, fair-faced, and irresistible.
Let him join these two first when the time for union has come—those by which the great power of the Asuras was conquered.
(1869) I cover your vital organs with armor; may King Soma clothe you with immortality.
May Varuṇa make for you a space wider than the wide; may the gods rejoice after you as you conquer. (1870)
May our enemies become blind and headless like snakes;
may Indra slay, one by one, those of you who have been driven away by fire.
Whoever—whether a kinsman, a stranger, or an outsider—seeks to kill us...

May all the gods strike him down; the sacred word (*brahman*) is my inner armor, my protection is my inner armor. Like a fearsome beast that wanders and dwells in the mountains, you have come from the furthest distance.
O Indra, having sharpened your bolt and made your blade keen, strike down the enemies and drive away the adversaries.

O Gods, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O Holy Ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious. With steady limbs and bodies, may we, offering praise, attain that lifespan ordained by the gods. May Indra, of far-reaching fame, grant us well-being; may Pūṣan, the knower of all, grant us well-being.
May Tārkṣya, whose wheel is unbroken, grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati grant us well-being.
Oṃ, may Bṛhaspati grant us well-being. Thus ends the Uttarārcika.
Thus ends the Saṃhitā of the Sāmaveda.
